name: Seasonal Youth Apprenticeship
org: 1001 Colors (Cincinnati public art and youth workforce development)
pay_detail: $13 an hour
duration: 8 weeks, June to July; 20 to 30 hours a week, Monday to Friday about 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
deadline_text: The 2026 Application and Interview Weekend has passed. The page says 2027 details will be posted by late 2026.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 21 years old at the start of employment. No prior professional experience is required.
how_to_apply: Complete the in-person application and interview during the scheduled Application and Interview Weekend.
notes: The organization's Gallery Fellowship (ages 16 to 24) and 10-month Mural Studio job are separate programs. The old ArtWorks web address now redirects to 1001colors.org. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: ACCEL Middle College (East Side Union / Evergreen Valley College)
org: East Side Union High School District
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)
duration: 2 years
deadline_text: Recruitment meetings are held in the evening; dates not posted on the page I read.
who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).

name: Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth)
grades: Currently in high school or college
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.
deadline_text: Ongoing
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Contact a regional provider: Eden Area ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. Main ACWDB line: (510) 259-3842.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead: La Familia (Eden Area) (925) 935-2643, Ohlone College (Tri Cities) (510) 742-2323, International Rescue Committee (North Cities) (510) 857-6884. See also Alameda County Youth Innovation Program, a separate listing from the same county board that names the same two providers (Eden ROP and Tri-Valley ROP).

name: Alameda County Youth Innovation Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Services include paid and unpaid work experience, so ask the provider about pay.
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who are currently in high school or college. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use a separate county youth program.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the program page: Eden ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. County line: 510-259-3842.
notes: Two providers only: Eden ROP (Hayward) and Tri-Valley ROP (Livermore), so which one serves you depends on where you live. Pay is not stated. A Hayward AJCC fact sheet (Rubicon Programs) mentions federal WIOA youth ages 14 to 24 with at least one barrier; ask your provider about younger teens. See also Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth), a separate listing from the same county board that names the same two providers.

name: After School Matters (paid apprenticeships and assistantships)
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 application opened Aug 26 and programs started Sept 28; no closing date stated and spaces are limited. Spring 2027 applications open in January; summer 2027 in April (per the session timeline).
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The fall page says the application is open, but programs began Sept 28, so confirm spots remain. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.

name: Discovery Station volunteer, Udvar-Hazy Center
org: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: At least 8 hours per month for one year
deadline_text: No application window stated; new openings are posted through the year.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older for Discovery Station and Astronomy volunteering (18 for most other roles). Commit to at least 8 hours a month for one year, preferably in 3-hour shifts.
how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' on the volunteer page, create an account in the museum's volunteer system, complete the orientation and online training, and sign a Program Volunteer Agreement.
notes: The Astronomy Education volunteer role (also 16+) was marked 'not recruiting at the moment'. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grader during the 2025-26 school year)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22-27, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 22-27, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadlines are not posted on the site.
who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade who are selected and sponsored by a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Each high school may have only one delegate. If a school has no sponsoring Unit, a student can apply as a Department (statewide) alternate applicant. Age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages read.

name: Alameda County Community Food Bank: Volunteer
duration: Shifts
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick a shift on the volunteer calendar.
who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.

name: Alameda County Library Teen Volunteers (Fremont, Newark, Union City)
city: Fremont, Newark and Union City, CA
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal. Not stated on the page I read.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. Phone 510-745-1500. The application link is on the official page.
notes: The teen page is thin. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
pay_detail: Community service hours only
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO)
pay_detail: Community service hours only
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the Teen Book Reviews page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.

name: Alameda Youth Career and Job Fair
org: City of Alameda and Alameda Unified School District
pay_detail: Free event
duration: One afternoon
deadline_text: The 10th annual fair was Wednesday, April 1, 2026, 1 to 5 pm. No 2027 date is posted.
who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.

name: Palefsky Collision Project (Alliance Theatre)
pay_detail: Free to all participants. No stipend mentioned.
duration: 3 weeks, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily (June 29 to July 17 in 2026, with performances July 17 and 18)
deadline_text: The interview and application window runs from January to mid-April each year; the Summer 2026 window is closed. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th graders, 12th graders and post-secondary students. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Apply during the window; the process includes an interview. The page encourages students to attend a performance and check back next year. Contact: collision.project@alliancetheatre.org or 404-733-4700.
notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.

name: Ann Arbor District Library Volunteer Program (teens and adults)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Ongoing; you commit to the shifts you sign up for
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply any time with the online form, then attend a volunteer orientation.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. After review you are contacted with details on signing up for a required volunteer orientation, then you pick shifts.
notes: Library does not offer court-ordered community service. Older library posts mention a summer teen volunteer program, but the current page only describes the year-round program. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Food Gatherers Volunteer Shifts (warehouse and Community Kitchen)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; you can volunteer as often as you like
deadline_text: Shifts open for sign-up 3 months ahead and fill quickly.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older to volunteer alone at the warehouse or Community Kitchen. Younger kids can come with an adult (warehouse 8 and up, kitchen 12 and up).
how_to_apply: Create a user account with Individual Registration and sign up for shifts in advance; no walk-ins. If you need school hours signed or an observer will attend, call the volunteer coordinator first.
notes: Not teen-specific, but a steady way for teens 14 and up to earn volunteer hours. Warehouse work involves moderate lifting. Groups of four or more use a separate group form. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Junior Volunteer Program at Humane Society of Huron Valley
pay_detail: $205 program fee for the 6 session training (training, T-shirt, supplies). Limited scholarships for families with financial need.
duration: 6 training sessions, then a 2 to 4 hour per month volunteer commitment
deadline_text: Registration for the November sessions (Nov 2 to 19) opens Mon Oct 19 at 8am; for the December sessions (Nov 30 to Dec 17) it opens Mon Nov 16 at 8am. Sessions are offered monthly and fill quickly.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 (must be 12 before registering). Those about to turn 18 within 6 months may prefer the adult orientation.
how_to_apply: Online registration only, which opens about 30 days before each session. You must attend all six classes; there are no make-ups, refunds or transfers. A waitlist is available.
notes: Demand is higher than space, so you may wait months. After training you volunteer without a parent present. Inactive for 6 months or more means retaking the training. Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: SummerWorks (Washtenaw County Summer Youth Employment Program)
org: SummerWorks: Michigan Works! Southeast, Washtenaw County OCED, University of Michigan Poverty Solutions and partners
pay_detail: Internships pay $15 or $17 per hour depending on whether you have finished high school or an equivalent (employer FAQ). About 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: Program runs April to August; internship is 10 weeks between June and August
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 15 and were due Mar 22, 2026; internship period June 15 to Aug 21, 2026. The site says 2027 applications open in mid-January and are usually open late January to late March. 2027 closing date is not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when programming begins (you must turn 16 by June 1 of the program year) AND you live in, or attend school in, Washtenaw County. Participants may take part for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Online application (opens January): your contact info, parent or guardian contact, approximate household income, possible summer conflicts, and one reference who is not a relative. Accepted minors need a parent or guardian signature.
notes: A paid internship is not guaranteed: the site says a subset of participants is selected, though staff aim to match everyone. After acceptance you need I-9 identification documents and a bank account in your name for pay (this is for payroll, not a fee). Professional development is Tuesday or Wednesday evenings online, then Fridays 10am to 2pm in person from June. Michigan requires a work permit for minors under 18 to work; as of Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state's Youth Employment Permit Portal, not schools. Contact: mail@summerworks.info.

name: Trinity Health Ann Arbor Teen Volunteer Program
org: Trinity Health Michigan, Ann Arbor and Livingston
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Year-round roles with some seasonal placements (a summer teen cohort exists)
deadline_text: No application dates posted. The 2026 Ann Arbor summer teen orientation was June 24, 2026, 11am to 4pm; no later orientation is listed.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Ann Arbor and Livingston volunteer page (the link goes to the hospital's volunteer system at stjoemercyann.vsysweb.com). Then an interview, paperwork, health screening and a required orientation.
notes: Requirements listed for volunteers: interview, two TB skin tests, proof of varicella and MMR immunity, Tdap, this year's flu shot, health clearance form, one non-relative reference, and orientation; background checks apply to volunteers 18 and over. Also on the same page: The Farm at Trinity Health takes volunteers age 15 and up (no background check under 18). The Apply Now link is http, not https, so it is not in the apply_url field. Volunteer office phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Youth Volunteer Corps and youth volunteer roles at the Ann Arbor YMCA
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies: one-off service projects or ongoing roles
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply any time with the volunteer application.
who_can_apply: The Youth Volunteer Corps is for teens ages 11 to 17. Ages for the other youth volunteer roles are not stated on the page. Youth sports coaches must be at least 14.
how_to_apply: Use the Begin your application button on the volunteering page. Questions: volunteer@annarborymca.org.
notes: The page's own link to a Youth Volunteer Corps page was a dead link when checked, so details of YVC projects and dates are not confirmed. The Y also lists other volunteer roles that appear aimed at adults. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: VolunTEENS at the Aquarium of the Pacific
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program (60 service hours).
duration: 60 hours over a 10-week session (Spring, Summer or Fall), one shift a day each week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 windows: Summer applications Mar 1 to Apr 15; Fall applications Jun 20 to Aug 5. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.

name: NextGen Youth Workforce Program (WorkSource Atlanta Regional)
org: Atlanta Regional Commission, Atlanta Regional Workforce Development Board
city: Cherokee, Clayton, Douglas, Fayette, Gwinnett, Henry and Rockdale counties, GA
pay_detail: The page does not mention wages, stipends or work experience pay. Ask your county provider what is offered.
duration: Year-round
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 living in Cherokee, Clayton, Douglas, Fayette, Gwinnett, Henry or Rockdale County. In-school or out-of-school youth who face a barrier such as offender history, homelessness, foster care, parenting, disability or being a basic-skills-deficient or English learner diploma holder.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Contact the provider for your county. Clayton: 770-997-4511 (640 Hwy 138 SW, Riverdale). Gwinnett: 404-913-0769 (3805 Crestwood Pkwy NW, Suite 300, Duluth). Cherokee: 770-345-5483. Henry: 404-913-0769. Douglas: 770-997-4511. Fayette: 770-910-7733. Rockdale: 770-991-7608.
notes: This is the only Gwinnett and Clayton county youth workforce program found. The City of Atlanta, Fulton, DeKalb and Cobb are not on this page's county list; see their own entries. Providers named on the page: Cherokee Youth Works and Hearts to Nourish Hope. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: TRIO Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math and Science (American River College)
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.
duration: Year-round, including a required summer component
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read, so ask staff for current dates.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
org: Arrowhead Regional Medical Center (San Bernardino County)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 100 hours; one 2-hour shift a week
deadline_text: No dates posted. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 and a half years old. The page lists this rule for all volunteers and links a separate Teen Volunteer Application.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Volunteer Application (Google form on the page). Questions: armc-volunteers@armc.sbcounty.gov or Volunteer Management, 400 N. Pepper Avenue, Colton, CA 92324.
notes: Minimum age is 14 and a half. The page lists no application deadline or start dates.

name: Teen Academy (summer art classes)
pay_detail: $185 per one-week course (Week 3 is $148). Morning (9 to 11:30 a.m.) and afternoon (12:30 to 3 p.m.) courses.
duration: Six weeks of themed courses (2026: June 1 to July 24)
deadline_text: The page shows the 2026 course schedule. 2027 dates and registration are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 years old. Students can join one week, all six or any number of weeks.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the registration link on the Teen Academy page. Questions: Office of Engagement.
notes: Courses change every week. Students agree to the handbook rules when they sign up. The page mentions scholarships; ask the Office of Engagement for details.

name: SPEAK Student Volunteers (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: 50 hours between June 2 and July 24 (2026), including a required 6-hour training day. Shifts Tuesday to Sunday in 2-hour blocks.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: info sessions Jan 13 and Feb 10, application and recommendation due March 1, 2026, group interviews March 21 or 28. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). Check the Garden volunteer page in December and January for the 2027 cycle.

name: Summer High School Internship (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: $12 per hour, paid every two weeks.
duration: 7 weeks (June 2 to July 16 in 2026), 18 hours a week, Tuesday through Thursday
deadline_text: The Garden says to check back in December 2026 for Summer 2027 details.
who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.

name: Atlanta Teen Leader Program and Parks and Recreation Teen Summer Employment
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Teen Leader activities are free. Pay for the summer employment program is not stated in the catalog.
duration: The 2026 Teen Leaders Summer Academy ran June 8 to July 24, Monday to Friday.
deadline_text: Register as a Teen Leader by Dec 31, 2026 to be considered for the Parks and Recreation summer employment program. That date is a registration cutoff, not a job application. Registration is ongoing. The catalog says summer 2026 employment registration is closed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 cutoff is for (most likely summer 2027). Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Labor and Employment Services
pay_detail: Paid. The page says competitive wages and does not state a rate.
duration: June 8 to July 16 in 2026 (about 6 weeks). Some positions may extend.
deadline_text: The 2026 program ran in June and July. Registration was a waiting list when we read the page. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.

name: City of Austin High School Summer Internship Programs
org: City of Austin, Austin Economic Development (Youth Initiatives)
grades: Rising sophomore, junior or senior, or current senior
pay_detail: $13 per hour, 20 hours per week
duration: 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Jan 28 to Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Austin, TX residents who attend an Austin-area high school, ages 15 to 18 when applying, available for the whole program with no more than 3 days absent.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link posted on the program page) with an essay. Choose your preferred track on the application. Email SummerHSIntern@austintexas.gov with questions.
notes: Separate from the Austin ISD / Austin Chamber paid internship. Placements depend on site access and career interest.

name: Teen Library Fellowship
org: Austin Public Library with the Austin Library Foundation
pay_detail: $21 per hour on the Foundation page ($22 per hour on the library pages), up to 10 hours of work per month
duration: 9 months (about August to May)
deadline_text: Foundation page: the next cohort application opens in May 2027. The 2026-27 application ran May 1-31, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 17 living in Central Texas who will be a sophomore, junior or senior in the coming fall (homeschoolers welcome). Must be able to work legally in the U.S., or be willing to waive pay on a student-only visa. About 10 teens are hired each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Foundation's Teen Library Fellowship page when the application opens. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at kathleen.houlihan@austintexas.gov.
notes: Fellows must attend a mandatory monthly Sunday afternoon retreat at the Central Library; travel stipends are available. The Foundation page says ages 15-17 and $21 per hour; library pages say $22 per hour and one library page says ages 15-18, so confirm when applications open.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall (Oct-Dec) and spring (Mar-May): 10 weeks, one 2-hour shift a week. Summer (June-July): 8 weeks, one 2 to 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Windows each year: fall Jul 1-31, spring Dec 1-31, summer Mar 1-31. The fall window has closed; the next one is spring, Dec 1-31 (the page gives these windows without a year).
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.

name: Caminos Teen Leadership Program
org: Emma S. Barrientos Mexican American Cultural Center (City of Austin)
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 6 to 10 hours per week
duration: 10 months, mid-to-late August through early June; most Saturdays 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. plus Wednesday evenings
deadline_text: Applications for the Class of 2027 are closed. The center will announce when applications reopen for the Class of 2028 on Instagram @atxcaminos.
who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. Dates for the next application window are not posted.

name: Lifeguard training and hiring

deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 16-19, with a parent's signed consent for 75 hours of intern service outside school, available to meet weekly.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application. All applicants get a follow-up email and some are invited to interview.
notes: The page does not say which library branches host councils. Whether a work permit is needed is not stated on the library page; ask the program.

name: Teaching Intern and Summer Volunteer
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.
duration: 6-week summer program
deadline_text: Not posted.
who_can_apply: The site says it recruits college and high school students as teaching interns. No age or grade rule is posted. Middle school students can also join as program students.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.

name: Volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: Only 16 and older. Younger teens should look at the Austin Public Library youth volunteer program (ages 13 to 17).

name: American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State)
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.
who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application: your school recommends you and a local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs: this one is coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program, ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. Old note about a 2020 article and Sanger phone was out of date.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 24 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet (this is the competition age rule). Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: Next-Gen Manufacturing Academy (High School Summer Academy)
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
duration: Club year
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.
who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Counted as school credit.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: Application is through the school that hosts the academy.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy sets its own application. Search the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy, or check nearby high schools. Whether students from other districts may transfer in depends on the district's open enrollment rules.
notes: The CDE site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (bot check), so this card could not be re-confirmed against the official page. Grades 10 to 12 and the school-within-a-school model need confirming. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Capital Area NextGen Youth Services
org: Capital Area Workforce Development Board (NCWorks Career Centers)
pay_detail: Apprenticeships and work experience are listed as services. Whether work experience is paid is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or enrollment status. Use the Complete an Interest Form button.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 in Wake and Johnston counties per the Capital Area youth page. The NextGen site says the program serves young adults facing barriers such as legal issues, home problems or missed education, and lists Wake, Johnston, Chatham, Lee and Orange counties. Exact eligibility rules and income limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form for your county at capitalareanextgen.org, or use the Request More Information form on the Capital Area youth page.
notes: This is the federal workforce (WIOA) style youth program for Wake County. Durham is covered by a different workforce board and is not listed. The pages do not say whether 14 to 17 year olds qualify in every case; ask the career center.

name: College Preview (pre-college art and design program)
pay_detail: Commuter $3,000 total ($2,750 tuition and fees plus a $250 registration fee). Residential $3,600 total (adds $600 room and board). Scholarships available.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
deadline_text: 2026 session: registration opened Nov 3, 2025, scholarship applications closed April 27, 2026, registration closed May 11, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12) interested in art and design.
how_to_apply: Register online and pay the $250 registration fee. Scholarship applicants submit a form, a 300 to 500 word personal statement, three artwork samples and a NACAC fee waiver.
notes: Fees shown are the 2026 prices. Meals are included on weekdays. Refunds: tuition balance less the registration fee is refunded in full if withdrawn by June 15, 2026 and half by June 29, 2026.

name: Supporting Student Success (WIOA In-School Youth)
org: Contra Costa County Office of Education
city: Contra Costa County, CA (West County and East County)
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Ongoing
who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.

name: Cedars-Sinai Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
deadline_text: 2027 sessions: Winter/Spring (Jan 25 to Apr 4) applications Nov 23, 2026; Summer (Jun 21 to Jul 25) applications Mar 29, 2027; Fall (Oct 4 to Dec 12) applications Aug 2, 2027. First come, first served; each application closes when spots fill.
who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.

name: Chabot College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, complete the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: cc-earlycollege@chabotcollege.edu or 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.

name: Galaxy Explorers Program
grades: Typically enters the summer before 10th grade and stays through 12th grade
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated, so needs_work_permit is null.

name: Carle Foundation Hospital Student Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: By term (fall, spring, summer)
deadline_text: Applications are due by 5 p.m. on August 29 (fall term), November 15 (spring term) or April 15 (summer term). The page gives no year.
who_can_apply: High school volunteers must be 14 or older. Students must provide up-to-date immunization records.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button under 'Students (college/teen)' on the Carle Foundation Hospital volunteer page (opens an online application) and send immunization records.
notes: The next listed deadline is the spring term deadline of November 15; confirm the year and current rules with Carle Volunteer Services. Other Carle sites list their own teen age ranges.

name: Youth Services (Workforce Development)
pay_detail: Not stated for youth. A separate Work Experience page says qualified interns can have up to 240 hours of wages covered.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: None stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who meet at least one condition, such as low family income, a disability, being a school dropout, homeless or foster youth, or needing extra help to finish school or get a job.
how_to_apply: The page gives no workNet address or walk-in hours. General CCRPC office: 1776 E Washington St, Urbana, IL 61802, (217) 328-3313.
notes: Eligibility rules apply, so not every teen qualifies. Call to ask about summer paid placements. The workforce site may be updated separately at eciwork.net. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: Counselor-in-Training, Summer Day Camps
pay_detail: Volunteer position.
duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
deadline_text: No application dates posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17. Candidates are picked through an application and interview.
how_to_apply: Email or call Stacey Clementz at the Homer Lake Interpretive Center, (217) 896-2455, or use the online volunteer application on the page.
notes: Youth program volunteers (school programs, September to May) and public program volunteers are also listed on the page; age rules for those are not stated. The District also has public volunteer events that need no application.

name: Champaign Park District Seasonal and Summer Jobs
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.
duration: Seasonal jobs run April to November and do not exceed 6 months; summer camp is a 10-week program
deadline_text: No application dates or deadlines listed on the page.
who_can_apply: The page says 15 year olds can apply for lifeguard and swim instructor. Minimum ages for other jobs are not stated; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the District's job listings (linked from the Employment Opportunities page). Aquatics questions: Ryan Hays, ryan.hays@champaignparks.org. HR: hr@champaignparks.org.
notes: Lifeguard classes are run by the District in Champaign-Urbana. Concession workers get a paid-for Food Handler's certification. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: Champaign Park District Teen Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteers register on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal.
who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 years old who are enthusiastic, hardworking and willing to learn. Teen volunteers may work at most 25 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal, then view opportunities. Questions: volunteer@champaignparks.org.
notes: Some roles (for example Prairie Farm) run only part of the year.

name: Dual Credit and Dual Enrollment at Parkland College
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask the Early College office.
who_can_apply: At least 15 years old, attending an area high school or home-schooled, with course prerequisites and assessment requirements met. For high school credit you also need your school's approval and good standing.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply page under Dual Credit. Early College Services: 217-353-2663, earlycollege@parkland.edu (office U214).
notes: Early College students do not qualify for financial aid. Credit and grades go on a permanent Parkland transcript. The Early College page also lists an Early College and Career Academy with programs such as Automotive Technology, Certified Nurse Assistant and EMS.

name: Champaign Public Library Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Typically 2 to 3 hours a week; a 4-month minimum is preferred
deadline_text: No deadline.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. If you are 16 or 17 you need a signed waiver from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application, then schedule the required interview. Contact: Eva Liu, Volunteer Coordinator, volunteer@champaign.org, 217-403-2000 x3.
notes: Open roles change, so look at the current listings on the page. The Douglass Branch's Club Fred program is a summer role.

name: Grainger Engineering Summer Camps
grades: Rising 7th to 12th grade. Individual camps have narrower ranges, such as 7th to 9th or 10th to 12th.
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $1,500, commuter $750, day camp $550, each plus a $25 deposit. The Trail Blazer Scholarship covers 50% or 100% for students who meet its criteria.
duration: One week per camp (June to August in 2026)
deadline_text: All 2026 camps are listed as full. 2027 application dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Pre-college students entering the listed grades in the fall. The page does not mention international students.
how_to_apply: Camp application (with the scholarship application inside it). See the Camp FAQs for the process.
notes: Costs do not include travel to campus. Some camps are EAGER or IDEA camps focused on broadening participation, open to all to apply. Use the WYSE mailing list for next year's dates.

name: Young Scholars STEMM Research Program
pay_detail: No cost except transportation. Housing, meals and a monetary award are provided (the page calls it a fellowship payment; the amount is not stated).
duration: 6 weeks (research began June 17 and ended July 31 in 2026); 30 to 35 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications Closed for Summer 2026.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who live in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa or Wisconsin. No international applicants. No course prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Online application with student information, two personal statements and a teacher, mentor or counselor recommendation form (emailed after you submit). Join the Summer Program Notifications mailing list for next year's dates.
notes: Competitive: applications are ranked together, not first come first served. Housing is for selected students who do not live locally. Students get no course credit.

name: Counselor-in-Training (CIT) Program
pay_detail: No wage is listed on the page; it is described as training for future summer and part-time jobs. Confirm with the contact.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week, three days a week, June 3 to July 31 in 2026 (8:15 am to 3 pm)
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who have completed 7th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application (PDF or online form on the Teen Programs page). Questions: Cathy Schneider (contact link on the page).
notes: Because pay is not stated, ask whether CITs are paid before applying. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: FRESH Crew Teen Volunteer Days
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn service hours and references.
duration: 2 hours per event (2 to 4 pm Saturdays)
deadline_text: No registration. Fall 2026 dates: Oct 3, Oct 17, Nov 7, Nov 21, Dec 5 (2 to 4 pm).
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. A parent or guardian must complete the Volunteer Waiver first.
how_to_apply: Show up. A guardian signs the Volunteer Waiver and emails it to Connor Ross (cjross@urbanaparks.org, 217-384-4062) or brings a printed copy on the day.
notes: Meets about every two weeks at different parks (Victory, Meadowbrook, Weaver, Crystal Lake, Busey Woods). The same page lists a free Teen Hangout Zone for grades 6 to 12 on select Fridays at Phillips Recreation Center.

name: Youth Event Support Volunteer
duration: Ongoing; most needed in summer and on afternoons and weekends in the school year
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: The library's volunteer interest form offers the age choices 14-17 and 18 and older. The page does not state a separate minimum age.
how_to_apply: Read the position descriptions, then fill out the volunteer interest form on the library's Volunteer with us page and pick Youth Event Support Volunteer.
notes: The 14 to 17 range comes from the age options on the interest form, not from a written rule. Call 919-968-2777 or email library@chapelhillnc.gov to confirm the minimum age and hours. The library also has a Teen Room for ages 13 to 18; no teen advisory board was listed on the pages read.

name: Community Attention Youth Internship Program (CAYIP)
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
deadline_text: The page lists four school-year sessions and one summer session for 2026-27 but gives dates only for Fall 2026 (applications Aug 20-28, 2026, now closed). For reference, the Summer 2025 application window was April 1 to May 1, 2025 (5 pm).
who_can_apply: Charlottesville-area youth 14 to 21 (14 by the start of the CAYIP Academy). City of Charlottesville residents get priority. Parent or guardian must also complete paperwork for youth under 18.
how_to_apply: Submit the CAYIP application (questionnaire, inventory and agreement to participate) during the session window, then a one-on-one interview. Accepted youth attend the mandatory paid CAYIP Academy. Contact: cayipinquiries@charlottesville.gov, 434-987-0018.
notes: Applications are only accepted during a session window. Transportation is not provided. Interns may miss at most 5 days per session. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers must get an Employment Certificate before any work; the program page does not mention it, so ask CAYIP staff how it is handled.

name: Lifeguard Training (Charlottesville Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Charlottesville Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Session dates were not listed on the page; use the Registration & Tickets link.
who_can_apply: Listed for ages 15 and up. Everyone must pass the in-water pretest or be removed from the class.
how_to_apply: Register through the city's Registration & Tickets system. Within 72 hours of registering, email swimprograms@charlottesville.gov with the subject Lifeguard Pretest to book the pretest at least 8 days ahead.
notes: The page does not say the class leads to a job. The city lists seasonal and variable-hour jobs on governmentjobs.com; none were open on 2026-10-09. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before any work.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
pay_detail: The program page does not state pay. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around a stipend.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site from the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page, or at a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.

how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.

The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
deadline_text: Rolling.

how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.

how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.

name: High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
deadline_text: The deadline for the Summer 2026 session has passed. The page says the summer application is usually posted in January, with about two months to finish the packet.
who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade. Seniors still in high school in spring must use the high school application.
how_to_apply: Submit the application packet by the posted due date, then attend a parent information session, an in-person interview and an orientation. Medical screening and a background check are required.
notes: Competitive: only the highest scoring applicants are accepted. Volunteers must complete at least 80 percent of their scheduled shifts. The hospital does not arrange job shadowing or senior capstone hours through Volunteer Services.

name: Aquatics Jobs: Lifeguard and Pool Staff
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. A 2026 lifeguard screening registration form is linked.
who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older, hold current American Red Cross Lifeguard Training/First Aid and CPR for the Professional Rescuer/AED certifications, and pass a water skills test. The page does not give an age for gate or pool monitors.
how_to_apply: Register for the required lifeguard course screening on the page, then apply to the open positions. Questions: CRC Aquatics, 513-357-7665.
notes: Lifeguards also attend pre-season and on-site pool training and pass an annual water skills review. Check the page for current screening dates. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Youth to Work (Y2WK) Summer Jobs
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the pages read
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
deadline_text: The program page says the application is usually available February to March. In 2026 the deadline passed in March (WVXU reported about two weeks left on March 10, 2026). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Live in the City of Cincinnati or a surrounding community and be 14 to 24. A limited number of positions are for ages 14 and 15. Under 18, a parent or guardian signs the hiring forms; under 16 you need a work permit.
how_to_apply: Create a free account at governmentjobs.com, then apply to the Y2WK job at agency.governmentjobs.com/cincinnati. Only online applications are accepted. Applicants are contacted by phone or email for an interview.
notes: Very competitive: WVXU reported more than 1,000 teens applied last year and about 6 percent were hired. The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Library Volunteer Opportunities (ages 12+)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week
deadline_text: The library volunteer system says it is accepting new volunteer applications. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Age 12 or older, able to commit to an ongoing schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for three months or longer. A background check applies at age 18 and older. Court-mandated volunteers are not accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill in an application in the library's online volunteer system and pick a listing. Questions: 513-369-6968.
notes: Each branch listing sets its own details, so check the age on the listing you choose. The page also mentions meal-service and tutoring roles and a separate Friends of the Library volunteer line at 513-369-6035.

name: Youth Programs Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
deadline_text: Youth volunteers are recruited each year from January through March. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, from public, private, parochial, charter and homeschool backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Use the youth application link on the Youth Programs page when recruitment opens. Email youthprograms@cincymuseum.org to be notified.
notes: The program started in 1989. In the first summer teens shadow the Museum of Natural History and Science, The Children's Museum and the Cincinnati History Museum.

name: Green Team Youth Summer Jobs
org: Groundwork Ohio River Valley with Cincinnati Parks
pay_detail: Paid summer job; rate not stated
duration: Summer; length not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the pages read. The City post is undated.
who_can_apply: High school students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Groundwork ORV Green Team page. Contact info@groundworkorv.org or 513-301-0310.
notes: Work sites named by the City include Mt. Echo Park, Mt. Airy Forest, Mt. Storm, Caldwell Nature Preserve and Kennedy Heights Park. Pay, hours and the application window are not on the pages, so ask Groundwork ORV. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: ZooTeen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application is open online Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027. Information sessions Nov 16, Dec 14 and Jan 11 (6 to 7 p.m.). Group interviews Feb 27, Feb 28, Mar 13 or Mar 14. Decisions by email April 2, 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. The page words the age rule as 13 to 17 on May 1, 2026, which looks like a leftover date for a 2027 season, so confirm.

name: FARMS Leadership Program

notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.

name: Urban Ag Internships

name: CTAE Work-Based Learning, Cobb County School District

notes: District CTAE and WBL coordinator on the page: Sapph Espinoza. The job should relate to your career goals and CTAE coursework. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: B.O.S.S. Young Professionals Program (CobbWorks)

duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.

who_can_apply: Cobb County residents ages 16 to 24 who meet income qualifications (decided at eligibility) and are in one of the program's target groups.
how_to_apply: Fill out the B.O.S.S. application inquiry form online (it asks if you live in Cobb County, are 16 to 24, and are in school), or call 770-528-4300 or email bossinfo@cobbworks.org.
notes: Funded through WIOA, so participants must meet eligibility rules. The same site lists a PowerUp! plumbing pre-apprenticeship and a Cobb County Fire P.R.E.P. Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: College of San Mateo Dual Enrollment and Concurrent Enrollment
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.

notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).

name: Summer Reading Challenge VolunTeen

how_to_apply: Online VolunTeen application, first come first served by branch. If your branch is missing from the drop-down, it is full.
notes: Openings vary by branch. Current or recent youth volunteers should talk to the Summer Reading coordinator at their branch. The library also has School Help, Reading Buddies and Creation Station volunteer roles; the page lists the age rule only for the summer VolunTeen role. Ohio's work permit rules for unpaid public library volunteering are not stated on the page.

name: Metro Parks Volunteer Program (Junior Volunteers at Inniswood)

how_to_apply: Attend a Volunteer Information session and complete the volunteer application. A background check including fingerprints is part of the process.
notes: Slate Run Living Historical Farm lets children volunteer with a parent or supervising adult. Scouts can set up group service days by email. For Inniswood contact the volunteer coordinator at 614-895-6226.

name: APPS Job Readiness Program

Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement. The page does not say how to submit the application beyond the schedule, so confirm the method with the program.

name: City Leaders Academy

name: Seasonal Lifeguard

notes: The City also offers Red Cross lifeguard training classes for ages 15 and older. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
