who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

name: STEAM Squad teen internship
pay_detail: Described as a hired position; the pay rate is not stated on the page
duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
deadline_text: Hiring dates are not stated. Sign up for Hennepin County job notifications to be told about openings.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the program page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Because hiring dates and pay are not on the page, confirm with the library before relying on it.

name: Teen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Ask your local library whether it has a teen opening.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Only a limited number of teen volunteer spots exist at some libraries.
how_to_apply: Ask your local Hennepin County library about teen openings. If there is one, fill out the teen volunteer application (PDF), bring it to the library, and a staff member will contact you. Questions: Volunteer Services, 612-543-8633.
notes: Adult volunteers have a different process. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

name: Hidden Genius Project Immersion Program
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed
duration: 15 months
deadline_text: The application page says applications are currently closed and to follow HGP social media or the newsletter for the 2027 application. The last posted deadline was Feb 21, 2025.
who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The immersion page still shows the old 2025 deadline. No 2027 date is posted, so wait for the new announcement. Oakland and Richmond are the East Bay sites.

name: Teen Leadership Council (High Museum of Art)
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
deadline_text: 2026-27 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed at midnight March 1 (2026); applicants were told by May 1, 2026. The page does not post the 2027-28 cycle.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.

name: Hiller Aviation Museum Flight Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.

name: Hire LA's Youth
org: City of Los Angeles Economic and Workforce Development Department (EWDD)
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
deadline_text: The site banner says it is accepting applications but gives no dates, and its document library page still shows a 2022 summer banner. Call EWDD at 213-744-7300 to confirm the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF we read (2024 version) lists the other eligibility rules, so check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before counting on a summer 2027 spot. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24 (school help, job readiness, some paid internships); ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit.

name: Hoag Jr. Auxiliary / Candystripers (High School Volunteer)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The program is full. The page says to check back January 2027 for when interest forms will be taken again.
who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. Specific weekly hours are not stated on the page.

name: Holy Cross Health volunteer program (high school students)
org: Holy Cross Health (Silver Spring and Germantown hospitals)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Not stated on the main page
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.
who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

name: Huntington Beach Public Library Teen Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
deadline_text: Most roles take online applications with no deadline. The Teen Tech role lists applications Aug 29 to Sep 12 and interviews Sep 15 to 18, but the page gives no year, so check the date.
who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens (Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center, OC Coastkeeper cleanups) with their own age rules, so read it for those. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.

name: Illinois Boys State (American Legion)
grades: High school juniors (finished at least one semester of 11th grade)
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
duration: One week, June 12 to 18, 2027 (90th annual session)
deadline_text: The registration page says registration for the 2027 session closes at 4:00 PM on June 12, 2027, when the session starts. Ask your local Legion post about its earlier sponsor deadline.
who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.

name: ALA Illini Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Illinois
city: Illinois (location not stated on the site)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages we read. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: Next session is June 20 to 26, 2027. The application deadline is not stated on the pages read; contact the Department office.
who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.

name: WorkOne young adult (youth) services
org: Indiana Department of Workforce Development, WorkOne Career Centers
city: Statewide, with WorkOne centers in Lafayette and other Indiana cities
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Contact a WorkOne center.
who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The Bloomington (South Central) WorkOne regional page was not read, so confirm locally. Call before going.

name: Inova high school student volunteer sessions
city: Fairfax, Alexandria and Northern Virginia hospitals, VA
grades: High school (through the summer after graduation)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 4 to Jun 20, 2027; 1 shift per week, 3 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 registration opens Nov 5, 2026 at 4 p.m. and closes Nov 8, 2026 at 11:45 p.m. Inova also runs summer and fall sessions.
who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 by the start of the session, interested in a healthcare career, and able to attend every session date. Needs a 250-word written response, background check, TB screening, MMR, varicella and Tdap proof, an interview with a parent, an in-person orientation and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Register during the window through the 'High school students register here' link on Inova's student page. Spots are assigned by lottery, one entry per applicant, and the student handles all email.
notes: Mandatory student-and-parent info meetings are in mid-November 2026 and orientations in late December 2026 (dates differ by hospital; one of each is required). Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Irvine Public Library Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
deadline_text: The undated page says: Summer Reading applications ran May 9 to May 30, school-year roles reopen Saturday, August 1, and TAG is full with a wait list for applications after August 26. No year is shown, so confirm current openings.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 (search for it on the volunteer system).

name: JA Launchpad (Junior Achievement, Fremont)
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)
deadline_text: The page says the center is Coming Early 2027. No opening date or sign-up is posted.
who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.

name: Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 18 (students in 6th grade or older). Boards meet at Central (1st Monday, 5 pm), Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial and Northside; Crozet is full and Gordon Avenue is not currently running.
how_to_apply: Use the Join a Teen Advisory Board page or contact your branch. The page does not say how to apply beyond that.
notes: Meeting times: Greene 1st Tuesday 4-5 pm; Louisa 3rd Thursday 3:45 pm; Nelson 2nd Thursday 4-5 pm; Northside 2nd Monday 7-8 pm. Gordon Avenue's entry on the teen volunteers page says its board is accepting applications while the TAB page says it is not currently running; call the branch.

name: Teen Volunteers at JMRL
duration: Varies by branch
deadline_text: The page gives a cutoff date for summer volunteer applications of 5/28/26 and does not say which branches it covers.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. Teen volunteers should be able to work independently. Branches include Central, Crozet, Gordon Avenue, Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial, Northside and Scottsville.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch (Send a Message link) or email the Young Adult Services Manager through the JMRL contact form. The page does not list formal application steps.
notes: Volunteering can count toward school or club service requirements. At the time of reading, Gordon Avenue said all weekly positions were filled. JMRL's volunteer coordinator is listed as Acacia Rodgers, volunteer@jmrl.org, 434-979-7151 ext 6695.

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.

name: John Muir Health High School Student Volunteer Program (Walnut Creek Medical Center)
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
deadline_text: No application window is stated on the official page. Contact a partner high school (for example Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, Miramonte, Monte Vista, San Ramon Valley or Ygnacio Valley) to ask about the next intake.
who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.

name: Junior Achievement of Northern California (high school programs)
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No central deadline; ask JA.
who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages read, so ask JA.

name: KP LAUNCH High School Program
city: Northern California Kaiser Permanente service areas
regions: silicon-valley; san-jose; peninsula; fremont; east-bay; oakland; san-francisco; sacramento
grades: Current high school student (priority to juniors and seniors) or Class of 2027 graduate
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
deadline_text: Opens Nov 16, 2026 at 9am Pacific; closes Jan 8, 2027 at 5pm Pacific.
who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive (a Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, not confirmed here). Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.

name: Kane County Workforce Development Youth Services (WIOA Youth)
city: Kane, DeKalb and Kendall Counties (Elgin area), IL
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No dates posted. You contact a provider and they explain how to start.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc.; Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.

name: King County Library System Teen Advisory Boards
city: King County, WA (branches outside the city of Seattle)

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.
how_to_apply: Contact your local librarian (Teen Services Librarian) or go to an open Teen Advisory Board meeting listed on the page. If your branch has no board, ask about starting one.
notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Key Club (high school service club)
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the pages read).
deadline_text: Join your school's club or start one. No cycle stated.
who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages read. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.

name: Khan Academy college and careers courses
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.

name: Kode With Klossy
city: Virtual and in-person (Oakland, San Francisco and more)
pay_detail: Free
duration: Code-a-Bration is 2 days; Camp is 2 weeks
deadline_text: Sign-ups are open for Code-a-Bration (Nov 7 to 8, 2026 in Oakland and virtual; Oct 17 to 18 in Chicago and virtual). Summer 2027 Camp applications open in February 2027; closing dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18; no prior experience required for the free onboarding programs. Camps run in several cities including San Francisco and Oakland, plus virtual.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.

name: LA County Library Teen Volunteer and Teen Advisory Board
org: County of Los Angeles Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.
duration: Varies by library
deadline_text: No deadline. Ask your local LA County Library about current openings.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.

name: LA County Youth@Work
org: LA County Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO)
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.
duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Fill out the youth interest form and an AJCC contacts you within 48 hours. In 2025 the summer jobs started July 1.
who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).

name: LACMA Teens
org: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort: applications ran July 1 to Aug 21, 2026 (5 p.m.) and are closed. The page says LACMA will not accept applications again until next year.
who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted; watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Whether the stipend counts as wages for work-permit purposes is not stated, so ask the program.

name: Zoo Teens (ages 14-17)
org: Columbian Park Zoo, City of Lafayette Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: Summer; shift details are in the 2026 Zoo Teen Information Packet (not read)
deadline_text: 2026 application closed; materials were due March 13, 2026. The zoo page says to check back in January 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 to 17 years old on June 1 of the year they apply. Teens interested in any career field may apply. A parent or guardian must co-sign the online application. A teacher or mentor recommendation form is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Read the Zoo Teen Information Packet, apply online through the zoo's volunteer form (applicant and parent both e-sign), and submit the teacher or mentor recommendation form. Contact: zooteen@lafayette.in.gov, 765-807-1543.
notes: Opening date for 2027 is not posted; the page only says check back in January 2027. The page mentions sponsors that keep costs low for participants but does not state a fee amount. The information packet was not read, so shift length and total hours are not stated here.

name: Summer College for High School Students (short-term residential courses)
org: Purdue University, Office of Summer and Winter Sessions
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: $60 application fee. Tuition and fees $347.85 per credit hour for Indiana residents ($948.30 nonresident). Room and board $377.95 for a 1-week program, $907.08 for 2 weeks. Some courses add $60 or $200 program fees. Scholarships exist.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, residential, June and July
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens December 1, 2026. Last cycle: priority deadline February 1, final deadline April 1. 2027 deadlines not posted.
