deadline_text: No deadline. The page says the online application is coming soon.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in south central Wisconsin (job centers in Dane, Sauk and Jefferson counties). Whether in-school youth qualify is not stated.
how_to_apply: Attend a free info session (listed on Eventbrite from the page), visit a Job Center, or call 608-249-9001.
notes: Eligibility rules (such as income) are not on the page, so call before you count on a paid placement.

name: Wisconsin Youth Apprenticeship (Dane and Jefferson counties)
org: Workforce Development Board of South Central Wisconsin
pay_detail: Paid while working; wage not stated.
duration: 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Virtual information nights (7:00 to 7:45 pm): Nov 18, 2026; Dec 16, 2026; Jan 20, 2027; Mar 17, 2027; and Feb 17, 2027 (UW Health sessions).
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in participating Dane and Jefferson county school districts. Employers choose and hire apprentices.
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's School to Career Coordinator (the page lists a name and phone for each district, for example Madison Metropolitan: Annie Johnston, 608-663-5384). Register for an information night on the program page.
notes: One date on the page is shown as Jan 20, 2027 even though its registration link says 2026, so check it. Students interested in UW Health need the Feb 17 session. Main office 608-249-9001. Ask the coordinator whether your age needs a Wisconsin work permit.

name: Major League Hacking (MLH) hackathons
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the pages read; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Weekend events; Fellowship is 12 weeks
deadline_text: Dates differ by event. See the 2027 season events list. California events listed: DiamondHacks (La Jolla, Apr 4 to 5, 2027) and LA Hacks (Los Angeles, Apr 16 to 18, 2027).
who_can_apply: Rules differ by event. On the 2027 events list only one event (hackPHS in New Jersey) is marked High School. The Fellowship page gives no age or student rule. Read each event page.
how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages read did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.

name: Teen Art Collective
org: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego (MCASD)
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications were due Friday Aug 28, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a late-summer deadline.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.

name: Teen Advisory Board at MCPL
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application, up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.
deadline_text: Rolling membership. The page is accepting applications for new members and states no deadline.
who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.

name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC), City of Menlo Park
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services Department
grades: Entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The 2026-27 window ran May through July 2026 (page lists a July 17, 2026 deadline). The next window is not announced.
who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.

name: EMPOWER Program (Merced County Office of Education)
pay_detail: Paid and/or unpaid work experience; wages are not stated.
duration: Not stated; follow-up services for at least 12 months after the program
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page; it has an online interest and application form.
who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 21 (for example, youth without a high school diploma). Teens 16 to 18 qualify only if they are out of school.
how_to_apply: Use the Click here to apply form on the EMPOWER page, or call 209-381-5926. The office is at 658 W. Main Street, Merced.
notes: Prospero (the Merced County workforce board, formerly WorkNet) lists EMPOWER as its main youth program for out-of-school youth. Prospero Youth Team: 209-724-2036. Confirm first: the page gives no start dates or wage.

name: Dual Enrollment and Merced College Classes (Merced Union High School District)
org: Merced Union High School District and Merced College
pay_detail: Free: students can take college courses at no cost, up to 11 units a semester. Textbook fees are waived for CCAP classes; textbook fees apply for concurrent enrollment.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No dates posted on the district page; check with your school's Pathway Counselor.
who_can_apply: Students in good academic standing at a Merced Union High School District school (Atwater, Buhach Colony, El Capitan, Golden Valley, Livingston, Merced, Sequoia, Yosemite). Complete the Merced College application, a parent consent form and a High School Permit.
how_to_apply: Apply to Merced College, submit the parent consent form and High School Permit, and talk to your school's Pathway Counselor.
notes: College privacy law applies once you enroll: parents do not get progress updates from Merced College. A college GPA below 2.0 can affect future college eligibility and financial aid.

name: Teen Library Volunteer
org: Montgomery-Floyd Regional Library (Blacksburg and Christiansburg branches)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Teens must be 11 or older. Volunteering is during the school year, with extra hours in summer for the Summer Reading Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: WIOA Youth Program through your local Michigan Works! agency
org: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, delivered by local Michigan Works! agencies (Michigan Works! Southeast for Washtenaw County, Capital Area Michigan Works! for the Lansing area)
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.
duration: Varies by local agency
deadline_text: Operated year round by local Michigan Works! agencies. No state deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675) or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org, then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.

name: Opportunity Youth Program, Middlesex College
pay_detail: Paid training and work experience are listed; the wage is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates listed.
who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Middlesex County and meet additional eligibility criteria. Not for teens currently enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Email opportunityyouthprogram@middlesexcollege.edu to start. Office: 550 Jersey Avenue, New Brunswick, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: The page does not name the funding source. Teens under 18 who are not in school should check eligibility with the office.

name: Milpitas Youth Advisory Commission
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)
deadline_text: The city says commission applications are accepted year-round, and appointments are made as needed. No closing date is stated.
who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.

name: Teens at Mingei
pay_detail: $750 for full participation
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications ran March 2 to April 1, 2026, with interviews April 20 to 24 and notices in August. Next cycle not posted; expect a similar spring window.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.

name: Step Up (Foundations level)
org: City of Minneapolis, Community Planning and Economic Development
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 window was Jan 5 to Mar 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted; the city says applications open each January and offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.

name: ZooTeen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
deadline_text: Applications for the Summer 2026 ZooTeen camp season are closed. The page says to check the website in 2027 for next summer.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. Follow the term dates.
who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

name: Montgomery County Recreation seasonal part-time jobs
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer camp positions fill in spring.
who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. A minimum age for these jobs is not stated on the page I read (it lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers).
how_to_apply: Use the 'Search and Apply' link on the Recreation employment page to apply for seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Summer RISE
org: Montgomery County Public Schools, Department of Partnerships
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Student registration opens in January and runs January to February (year not stated on the page). Placements are announced in April or May.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Because it is a stipend (if funded) role, ask your school counselor whether a Maryland work permit applies. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: TeenWorks Employment Program
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
deadline_text: Application windows on the page: Jan 2 to Mar 30 (spring/summer) and Aug 1 to Nov 30 (fall/winter). The page does not state the year, so the fall/winter window may be open now.
who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the program page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 Teen Summer Volunteer Program open in late winter or early spring 2027. No closing date posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

name: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated
duration: School year, August to June
deadline_text: Page still shows an 'Apply now for 2026-2027' banner but gives no closing date; applications opened Feb 6, 2026. Recruitment for the next school year opens each February.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the city YAC page. Questions: yac@mountainview.gov or 650-903-6331.
notes: Meets twice a month, August to June, at 4:30 p.m. in person at The View Teen Center, 263 Escuela Ave. Email to ask whether 2026-27 seats are still open.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)
org: Metropolitan Transportation Commission (with ABAG, BCDC and the Bay Area Air District)
city: Bay Area (virtual sessions, final session in San Francisco)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after completion; amount not stated
duration: 2026: virtual Thursday evening sessions in July plus a final in-person session at Bay Area Metro Center, San Francisco (July 31, 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 program is over. The 2026 call was announced March 24, 2026; exact open and close dates are not on the page. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: Bay Area residents who attend a local high school, are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade before it starts. Parent or guardian permission is needed under 18. GPA is not considered.
how_to_apply: Contact Academy@BayAreaMetro.Gov or 415-778-5207. The page does not detail the application steps.
notes: MTC's older 'High School Internship Program' pages date to 2018; the high school program MTC lists now is this Academy. It is mostly virtual evening sessions, not a job placement.

name: Summer Camp Youth Volunteer
duration: Camp weeks; schedule not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No 2027 deadline posted on the pages read. Check with the museum in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Youth volunteers ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply through the museum's volunteer portal (MyImpactPage) via the Learn more link on the Volunteer page. General museum volunteer steps listed: application, background check, new volunteer orientation. Questions: volunteer@lifeandscience.org.
notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).

name: NAACP/JMRL Paid Library Internship and Scholarship
org: Jefferson-Madison Regional Library and Albemarle-Charlottesville NAACP
grades: Entering 12th grade, or age 17 or older
pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)
duration: 200 hours of library work
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications due 5 pm, March 27, 2026; award announced by April 30, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Residents of Albemarle, Charlottesville, Greene, Louisa or Nelson who are at least 17 or entering 12th grade. High school applicants need a college admittance letter or a counselor letter showing they plan to attend college.
how_to_apply: Submit an application form, an essay of at least 300 words, transcripts with GPA, a resume, a college letter, and two reference letters from non-family members, to director@jmrl.org or to the Library Director, 201 East Market St, Charlottesville.
notes: The official source read is the 2026 program flyer (PDF) on jmrl.org; the library's other pages did not list this internship. An applicant cannot receive the award more than twice. Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).

name: NASA Citizen Science Projects
pay_detail: Free
duration: Whenever you want
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.

name: NASA GeneLab for High Schools (GL4HS)
city: Virtual (hosted by NASA Ames, Mountain View, CA)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (and college freshmen)
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026, or until 1,000 applicants. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.

name: High School Career Academy
pay_detail: Paid; amount not stated
duration: November to April; two evening sessions a month (4:30 to 8 p.m.)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026-2027 is closed. 2027-28 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Franklin County and surrounding areas.
how_to_apply: Register when the program reopens; contact HNHFWorkforceDev@nationwidechildrens.org.
notes: The hospital's student opportunities page also lists Project SEARCH (a 9-month internship for students with disabilities) and Upward Bound Math and Science. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Youth and Young Adult Employment Program (paid summer work experience)
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated
duration: 4 or 8 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 30)
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Feb 2 and closed March 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 21. Participants must be at least 16 years old at the time of registration.
how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.

name: Junior Curators
org: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
pay_detail: $75 per year (snacks, T-shirt, boots and protective eyewear); optional trips may cost extra for travel
duration: September to April. One monthly meeting with Living Collections staff plus two monthly group meetings with scientists (3:30-5 pm).
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period has closed. Applications reopen in January 2027 and are due in March 2027 for 2027-28 (exact day not posted).
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. The school calendar followed is Wake County's; the page does not say whether eligibility is limited to the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: The page gives no step-by-step process. Staff contact is Lynn Cross (listed on the page).
notes: Selection criteria were not described on the page.

name: Junior Interpreters
org: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
pay_detail: $75 per summer (covers orientation, food, T-shirt, nametag and props)
duration: 10 weeks, June 15 to August 19. One shift a week (Tue, Wed or Thu, 10-1 or 1-4). Required orientation Saturday May 15.
deadline_text: Applications open mid-January 2027 and are due 5 pm Monday, March 22, 2027. Group interviews April 13-15, 2027, 3:30 to 5:00 pm; top applicants are invited.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders. The museum's general volunteer rule is 18 and older; under-18s join through the teen programs.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in mid-January 2027, then attend a group interview if invited. The page does not describe the application steps; contact the listed staff member.
notes: Teens may reschedule up to 3 of the 10 shifts. Other teen programs on the museum's Teens page (Climate Resilience Institute, Cafe Coordinators, Teen Science Cafes) were listed without dates or fees.

name: NC State Rising 11th-12th Grade Residential Engineering Camps
org: NC State College of Engineering, The Engineering Place
pay_detail: $1,550 camp fee in 2026, no refunds. A limited amount of financial aid is available for demonstrated need.
duration: 1 week (2026 weeks: June 14-19, June 21-26, July 5-10, July 12-17)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: portal open January 12 to February 27, 2026; decisions March 27, 2026. The page says to watch for 2027 camp information.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade (2026 page). Homeschooled, out-of-state and international students are encouraged to apply. Admission is based on academics (typically A's and B's in math and science) and interest.
how_to_apply: Online application: GPA, school and counselor info, and two short written answers (camp goals and a problem you would like to solve). Each applicant is placed in one workshop.
notes: All dates and the fee on the page are for 2026; 2027 terms were not posted. The Engineering Place also runs day camps for younger students.

name: Soup Kitchen Volunteering, Elijah's Promise
pay_detail: Unpaid. Court-ordered service hours are not accepted.
duration: One shift at a time, Monday to Saturday between 8:00 am and 12:30 pm
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts online; if none show, they are filled.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 18 must come with a guardian, and you must secure an individual volunteer slot for both the adult and child.
how_to_apply: Register for a shift on the volunteer site linked from the page; a minor and the supervising adult each need their own slot. Questions: volunteer@elijahspromise.org or 732-545-9002 ext. 122.
notes: Wear closed-toed shoes and long pants; expect to stand for the whole shift. Only five people fit in the kitchen at once. Large groups are booked through January 2027.

name: Rutgers 4-H STEM Ambassadors Program
grades: Entering 9th or 10th grade (apply in 8th or 9th grade)
pay_detail: Free: direct summer program expenses are paid by a scholarship valued at $1,000. No wage or stipend is listed.
duration: Year-round, multi-year; 2026 summer program at Rutgers-New Brunswick was July 6 to 10
deadline_text: 2026 cohort application closed. The page says check back in early 2027 for the next cohort.
who_can_apply: College-bound youth from urban communities in Atlantic, Camden, Essex, Hudson, Mercer, Middlesex, Passaic and Union counties, with a B or better GPA, top 25% of the class, and interest in volunteering to help 4-H with STEM programs.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program site (opens early in the year). About 60 students are accepted each year. Contact on the Rutgers 4-H STEM site: Chad Ripberger, ripberger@njaes.rutgers.edu.
notes: Only students in the listed counties qualify. Selected students start with an orientation in May and two short online modules.

name: Rutgers Summer Scholars Program
org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick Pre-College Summer Programs
grades: Current high school students (graduating seniors not eligible)
pay_detail: 2026 rates per credit: in-state $482 (Arts and Sciences) to $551 (SEBS), out-of-state $1,148 to $1,338, plus a one-time $162 student fee. Courses are typically 3 credits; up to two courses.
duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened February 2; last day to apply May 17 (Session I) and June 28 (Session II). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school students ages 16 to 18 (must be 16 by the course start date) with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Graduating seniors are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus unweighted transcript, a Parent/Guardian Permission Form and a letter of recommendation (teacher or anyone who knows your work). Reviewed first come, first served; decisions in 5 to 7 business days.
notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.

name: Toxicology, Health and Environmental Disease (THED) High School Summer Program
org: Rutgers Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences Institute (EOHSI)
grades: Entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in fall 2026, with at least one high school biology course
pay_detail: $975 non-refundable camp fee covers tuition, manuals, materials, safety equipment, lab supplies and lunch. Need-based financial aid may be available. No housing or transportation provided; no stipend.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: enrollment opened January 5, 2026; deadline was Monday, March 2, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Motivated high school students entering grades 10 to 12 who have completed at least one high school biology course.
how_to_apply: Online application only: about 250-word essay on your interest, high school transcripts or report cards, and your preferred session. Acceptance emails go out in the first week of April; pay within 2 weeks to hold the spot.
notes: Held at EOHSI, 170 Frelinghuysen Road, Piscataway. Questions: THED@eohsi.rutgers.edu. Expect the 2027 cycle to follow the same winter pattern, but confirm on the page.

name: Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
deadline_text: 2026: reviewed first come, first served from February 2026; completed application, including solutions to the problems, by March 31 if seeking a scholarship; financial aid applications by April 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Mathematically talented high school students. No specific grade or age is listed. You must submit solutions to the Problems to Explore.
how_to_apply: Four parts: Student Information and Consent Google Form (with a parent), your solutions to the Problems to Explore, a teacher recommendation emailed directly, and a transcript emailed by your counselor.
notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. Page read was the Summer 2026 listing.

name: Teen / High School Volunteers, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
org: RWJBarnabas Health, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
deadline_text: No application deadline or dates are listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who have completed ninth grade. Weekday shifts are 4 to 6 p.m. for ages 15 and up, or 6 to 8 p.m. for ages 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Director (Jacob.Persily@rwjbh.org) with the teen's name, high school and current grade. Applications are not sent at a parent's request. Then orientation, medical clearance (health form from a doctor covering TB screening, immunizations and flu vaccine) and a drug screen. Phone: 732-937-8507.
notes: Volunteers must be fully vaccinated and wear the provided uniform. The page says internships and shadowing are not offered. A newer and an older version of this page disagreed on hours (75 vs 100 a year); the page read on 2026-10-09 says 100.

name: Waksman Institute Summer Experience (WISE)
org: Waksman Institute of Microbiology, Rutgers University
grades: High school students who completed a high school biology course
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
deadline_text: 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and was first come, first served (sessions expected to fill). Application forms for the Summer 2027 WISE Programs will be posted in late January 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed a high school level biology course. No age or grade range is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the WISE page; first come, first served. Pay the fee within 2 weeks of approval.
notes: In-person sessions are non-residential at the Waksman Institute on the Busch campus in Piscataway. The year-long Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP) is a separate, school-based program that starts with teachers.

name: Governor's School of New Jersey in Engineering and Technology
org: Rutgers School of Engineering / State of New Jersey
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
deadline_text: 2027 application not posted on the pages read. The state page (updated 11/13/25) said 2026 applications were open; decisions are emailed in early April. Ask your school counselor about the school nomination deadline.
who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). Competitive: fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.
who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the program page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.

name: Waterpark seasonal jobs with free training
org: NOVA Parks (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority)
city: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Alexandria and Arlington waterparks)
pay_detail: Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
deadline_text: Page says NOVA Parks is hiring; no deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page read does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income plus justice involvement, unstable housing or foster care.
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. Most applicants need a documented barrier and income under the program limits.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.

name: Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
deadline_text: Submit your materials before Dec 4, 2026 to be invited to an interview. No final deadline is posted. Info session Sat Oct 17, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. You do not have to share immigration status for Tiers 1 to 3.
how_to_apply: Apply online (account lets you save progress): short answers plus references, then a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the program page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.

name: Pre-College Programs: NYC Commuter Summer
org: Columbia University School of Professional Studies
grades: Entering grades 9 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: 1-week session $2,883. 3-week session $6,381. Plus an $95 application fee and $50 or more for course materials. Deposit $1,000 (1-week) or $2,000 (3-week) is credited toward the cost. These are estimates pending trustee approval.
duration: 1 week (Jun 21 to 25, 2027) or 3 weeks (Jun 28 to Jul 16, 2027; more sessions listed on the dates page).
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open mid-November 2026. Early registration deadline Feb 1, 2027. General application deadline Apr 1, 2027 for the NYC Commuter sessions.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 or freshman year of college. The commuter option is for students who live in or near NYC. Academic strength is what the admissions team looks for.
how_to_apply: Online application. Columbia says applications are reviewed on the dates-and-deadlines schedule; early registration is cheaper to plan around.
notes: Expensive; the page says financial aid details are elsewhere and they were not read. The commuter page still shows a $95 application fee under a Summer 2026 cost heading while the cost page for Summer 2027 says $80. Free Columbia programs for NYC teens (Double Discovery Center, Freedom and Citizenship) exist but their pages blocked access, so they are not listed.

name: Summer Innovation Intensives
grades: Finished sophomore year of high school or later
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page (students earn 2 Cornell credits). Ask summer@tech.cornell.edu before applying.
duration: 3 weeks, commuter only (no housing). Exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The summer 2027 application will open in winter 2026. The summer 2026 application is closed. No deadline posted. Rolling review.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 19 who completed 10th grade by the program start, live in the NYC area (or arrange a supervising adult and housing), and are U.S. citizens or permanent residents at U.S. curriculum schools. No interview or minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript, two recommendation letters and short essays (250 to 300 words each). Contact: summer@tech.cornell.edu.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page read, so confirm the price and any financial aid with the program before applying. Selective. International students are not admitted at this time.

name: Ladders for Leaders
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
grades: Rising high school seniors and college students
pay_detail: At least $16.50 per hour in 2025 (2025 FAQ). 2026 pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 6 weeks, 25 to 40 hours a week (2025 FAQ)
deadline_text: DYCD page says the deadline for the last cycle was extended to January 16, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: 2025 FAQ: rising high school seniors or college students ages 16 to 24 who can legally work in the U.S. and have some prior paid or volunteer work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the SYEP application online at application.nycsyep.com and choose a Ladders community partner. Selection uses a personal statement, transcript and resume, then workshops, mock interviews and employer interviews (2025 FAQ).
notes: Competitive. Eligibility, pay and process come from the 2025 FAQ because no newer FAQ was found, so check the DYCD page when applications reopen. Interns under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). Free to apply.

name: Learn & Earn
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: Paid six-week summer internship. Rate not stated on the page.
duration: Year-round program with a six-week paid summer internship
deadline_text: Page says enrollment dates are September 1 to 30 (year not stated). That window has passed for this fall.
who_can_apply: NYC high school juniors and seniors who live in New York City, are low income (or meet an exception such as public assistance, foster care or living in a high-poverty area) and meet at least one other listed need. The page lists age 16 to 21 in one place and 14 to 21 in another, so ask a provider.
how_to_apply: Contact a Learn & Earn provider from the DYCD list, or call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646. Providers check your eligibility.
notes: Income-based, with extra eligibility rules listed on the page. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: Ages 16-24 (2026): $17.00 per hour, 25 hours a week. Ages 14-15 (2026): up to $700 for about 12.5 hours a week.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed March 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who live in the five boroughs of NYC and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. Some options (school-based, NYCHA, foster care, homeless youth) have extra rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com or on paper with an SYEP provider. One application only. Community-based placements are picked by random lottery. Have ID documents ready (proof of age, identity, address, Social Security).
notes: Pay and hours above are the 2026 numbers and may change. Free to apply. NYS Department of Labor says anyone 14-17 needs working papers (employment certificate) to hold a job in New York State; ask your SYEP provider what they need from you. Teens in school-based (CareerReady) options apply through their school. You pay your own transportation and meals.

name: Work, Learn & Grow (WLG)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: New York State minimum wage, paid every two weeks (DYCD FAQ).
duration: 22 weeks, Oct 26, 2026 to Apr 3, 2027, 250 hours total
deadline_text: The WLG application page lists a deadline of October 9, 2026. The FAQ PDF lists the application period as Sept 8 to Oct 2, 2026, so confirm with your SYEP provider.
who_can_apply: NYC residents legally allowed to work in the U.S. who took part in the 2026 Summer Youth Employment Program as CareerReady (ages 16 to 19 in a CareerReady partner high school) or in Special Initiatives (ages 16 to 20, in high school or a high school equivalency program), as of Oct 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the WLG online application (CareerReady or Special Initiatives link), or ask your SYEP provider for help. If selected, submit documents online or in person to your provider.
notes: Only for teens who were in 2026 SYEP through a partner school or Special Initiatives provider, so most teens cannot start here. Internet access is required. Closing today or very soon as of the verification date. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).

name: Summer Volunteer Program for High School Students
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Summer session runs June to September; minimum 100 hours; each session at least 3 to 4 hours.
deadline_text: The page still shows Summer 2025 postings with high school applications January 1 to May 31. No 2027 dates are posted. Onboarding takes about a month, so apply early in spring.
who_can_apply: Students 16 and older (some roles, such as Maternal Child Health, require 18). Montefiore also partners with SYEP; its SYEP provider is Children's Arts and Sciences Workshop.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Summer Volunteer - High School posting on Montefiore's career site (linked from the volunteer page), then attend an orientation and interview. Interviews are first come, first served.
notes: Confirm first: the dates are from the 2025 posting. Contact: volunteerservices@montefiore.org (shown on the page).

name: Junior Medical Program (JuMP) and high school volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no JuMP cost or pay.
duration: JuMP: 6 weeks, 100 hours. Unit Support: one 3-hour shift a week; the page lists a 100 hour minimum for high school students.
deadline_text: JuMP applications are accepted January 1 to March 1 (no year given on the page; expect Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2027). Space is limited. The process can take 4 to 8 weeks.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. JuMP is for ages 15 to 17 and requires full availability for all six weeks. Unit Support is open to high school students. The emergency department and some other roles are 18+.
how_to_apply: Online application, one letter of recommendation from a non-relative, and a resume.
notes: Read through the fetch tool because direct downloads were blocked. The page says volunteers need a valid Social Security number (a hospital clearance rule on the official site) and pay for their own medical clearance. Other Mount Sinai campuses have their own pages and age rules that were not read.

name: NYBG High School Explainer Program
pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.
duration: Spring 2027 internship: one 4.5 hour Saturday or Sunday shift each week, Mar 20 to Jun 19, 2027 (minimum 105 service hours), plus 4 required training days (Mar 6, 7, 13, 14, 2027).
deadline_text: Spring 2027 application closes Saturday Nov 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Open House Sat Nov 7, 2026, 1 to 2 p.m. (RSVP by Oct 30). A fall session also runs; its applications open late spring.
who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12. The application form says weekday internship options are only for Partnership School students, so check which options you can apply for.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Complete applications get an invite to a group interview at the Children's Adventure Garden. Accepted teens attend orientation with a parent or guardian and 24 hours of training before starting.
notes: Questions: explainers@nybg.org. Intern tier is unpaid, so a work permit is not clearly needed there; the paid tiers are jobs and the page does not say what papers are required. The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.

name: Summer Only Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Minimum 120 service hours over the summer.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted January 1 to March 31 (the page gives no year; expect Jan 1 to Mar 31, 2027).
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 (18 for some programs; check each campus). The Queens and Hudson Valley campuses do not offer Summer Only volunteering. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application and choose Summer Only plus your preferred program and campus. A volunteer services representative contacts you for an interview if a spot is open.
notes: Many NYP roles (emergency department, palliative care and others) are 18+. Brooklyn Methodist also runs a Junior Volunteer Program that was marked full when searched; its own page was not read for details. This entry covers the system-wide Summer Only option only.

name: Summer Volunteer Program, Manhattan Campus
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says no pay or school credit is given.
duration: 8 weeks, two 6-hour shifts a week (100 service hours total).
deadline_text: Applications open annually January 15 to February 15 (or until capacity is reached). The page gives no year; expect Jan 15 to Feb 15, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old at the start of the program. Under 18 cannot volunteer during the school year. The year-round program is 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Online application, a group information session, full summer availability, onboarding, health clearance (TB test, MMR and varicella proof, flu shot) and a background check.
notes: The Brooklyn campus requires age 18+. Long Island has its own teen program (not read in detail). The FAQ page still shows old 2022 dates, so only the Manhattan page was used for dates. Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org.

name: ARISE (Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (10th or 11th graders applying)
pay_detail: Free. A $2,000 stipend is paid for completing the program.
duration: 10 weeks: about 4 weeks of remote after-school workshops in June, then 6 weeks of in-person lab work (about 150 hours of lab experience). Summer 2026 ran Jun 1 to Aug 14, 2026.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 deadline was Feb 27, 2026 at 5 p.m. Summer 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Full-time NYC residents who attend NYC schools, applying as 10th or 11th graders (rising juniors and seniors), with strong grades and interest in STEM. Students from groups underrepresented in STEM are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Online application (optional recommendation due after), a group interview and lab tours to pick your placement.
notes: Selective with limited spaces. Funded by the Pinkerton Foundation. Students present at an AMNH poster symposium at the end. The two NYU pages differ slightly on grade wording (10th or 11th grade now versus rising juniors and seniors), which is the same group. The program name on a second page reads Applied Research In Science and Engineering.

name: Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
grades: Current high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: Applications for SSRP 2027 open Oct 15, 2026. The deadline is not posted yet. The last cycle closed Fri Jan 2, 2026 (letters of recommendation due Jan 5), with Zoom interviews in March and decisions in April.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to confirm you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. The program page labels its glance box SSRP 2026 but lists the 2027 dates. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.

name: Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program
org: Wildlife Conservation Society (Bronx Zoo, Central Park, Prospect Park and Queens Zoos, New York Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
deadline_text: Not accepting applications now. Applications for the next cycle open in late December 2026 for Spring 2027. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.

name: Youth Insights (YI Artists, Arts Careers, Introductions, Leaders)
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (varies by program; YI Leaders is grades 11 and 12)
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
deadline_text: YI Artists (this semester) deadline was Sep 9, 2026 (extended). YI Arts Careers and YI Introductions list no 2026 deadline and reopen in Summer 2027. No YI Leaders deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders, which conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact; use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE) high schools
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
deadline_text: Enroll through the regular NYC high school admissions process. Dates are not stated on the CTE page.
who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.

name: Career Readiness and Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA)
org: NYC Public Schools with CareerWise New York
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
deadline_text: Dates are not stated. Juniors apply during the school year; ask your school.
who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Oakland, Oakland Workforce Development Board, and partner nonprofits
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Advisory Board (TAB)

deadline_text: Rolling

notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week
deadline_text: Rolling. Not every branch has space at all times.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.

name: Teen Summer Internship (California Trail Interpretation)
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.

deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted.

how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.

name: Teen Wild Guides
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 info meetings Aug 15 and 16, applications due Sept 1, 2026, trainings Sept 26 and Oct 4. The page says applications are accepted year-round and later ones are reviewed in the next enrollment period.
who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season. Zoo page lists grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.

name: ZooCamp Teen Assistant and Teen Interns
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.
duration: 1-week sessions, Mon to Fri, June 1 to Aug 7 (2026); at least 3 sessions (Administrative Intern: 3 sessions in a row)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed April 1, 2026 at 5pm. Summer 2027 dates not posted yet; the page says to check back.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 for Teen Assistant (no experience needed). Paid Teacher and Administrative Intern roles are for grades 11 to 12 with previous camp experience and one letter of recommendation. All roles need at least 3 one-week sessions.
how_to_apply: Each role has its own online application (Volgistics link on the Oakland Zoo page). Interns also need one recommendation letter. A required training day is held in May.
notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.

name: OC Fair & Event Center Jobs (annual OC Fair)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
deadline_text: No hiring dates posted on the jobs page for 2027.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.

name: OC Public Libraries Teen Volunteer
city: Orange County, CA (any OC Public Libraries branch)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings are limited and depend on each branch.
who_can_apply: Teens are typically 12 to 17, but each branch sets its own age range, so check with your local branch. Court-ordered community service is not offered.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.

name: OC Workforce Development Board READY S.E.T. OC (WIOA Young Adult Program)
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Start by filling out the interest form.
who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.

name: OUSD Linked Learning Internships
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
fields: any; health; tech-cs; arts-media; engineering; business-finance

notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.

name: OUSD Linked Learning: Pathways, Internships and Work Permits
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

notes: The office handles work permits (needed for any paid job under 18). Check the pathways pages on the OUSD site to find work-based learning at your school.

name: Palo Alto Art Center Summer Camp Counselor in Training
org: City of Palo Alto Art Center
duration: At least 1 week
deadline_text: CIT and Lead CIT registration opens Feb 4, 2027 with Enjoy! summer camp registration. No closing date stated.

notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.

name: Teen Library Advisory Board (Palo Alto City Library)

deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in December 2026 to apply for Winter/Spring 2027.

notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.

name: Teen Advisory Board (Mitchell Park Teen Services)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
deadline_text: The page mentions a deadline but gives no date or year. The only dates found were in a 2023 city article.

how_to_apply: Submit the online application, recommendation letter and intro video by the deadline, then interview with the nominating committee.
notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

name: Palo Alto Youth Council (PAYC)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
deadline_text: The page says the application opens July 2027. No closing date stated.

notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

name: Pathful Explore (virtual career exploration)

notes: The home page names Pathful and Pathful Junior and does not use the name Pathful Explore. It is a school-run tool; individual students likely cannot join without a school plan.

notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers including incoming 9th graders (2026 dates were June 22 to July 31; no application deadline posted). The old OUSD page mentions a stipend; the Peralta page does not.

name: Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP)
org: Prince George's County Government, Office of Human Resources Management

notes: Facts come from the County Executive's official March 1, 2026 bulletin; the county SYEP web pages returned Access Denied to my reader, so confirm at syep.mypgc.us. Highly in demand, so apply the day the window opens. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Youth volunteers at Summer Playtime and Summer Day Camps

notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Library volunteering and VolunTEEN

notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Volunteer Program, Academy of Natural Sciences
org: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University

how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.

name: Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI)
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support

notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the program page.

name: Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L-PHL) Summer Program
org: City of Philadelphia Office of Children and Families, with JEVS Human Services

how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit if applicable. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Work permit listed only as 'if applicable'.

name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was April 3, 2026. The page says 2027 Summer Institutes information will be posted this winter.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.

name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.

deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.
who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
deadline_text: Free training is offered year-round; reserve a slot on Eventbrite.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).

name: Parks and Rec Summer Youth Employment Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Summer
deadline_text: The page still says registration closed for the C2L-PHL Summer 2025 program. No 2026 or 2027 dates posted.

how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page I read had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.

name: PYNtern Program

how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE), School District of Philadelphia

name: Counselor-in-Training Program, Camp Schuylkill

how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.

name: Wildlife Clinic Support Volunteer, Schuylkill Center

how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form linked on the page.

name: Teen Volunteer Program, Piscataway Public Library
grades: Grades 6 to 12 (high school volunteers: grades 9 to 12 and at least 14)

duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training

name: CS Scholars

name: Pomona College Academy for Youth Success (PAYS)
