who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 18 who live in one of eight listed North Natomas apartment complexes (address checked in week one).
how_to_apply: Register through ActiveNet using the Register Here button when a session is open. NNworkforce@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for residents of the eight eligible apartment complexes (Atrium Court, Natomas Park, Terracina Gold, Terracina Meadows, The Lofts, Valencia Point, Westview Ranch, Willow Glen). You must meet the age rule by the session start date. Only one absence is allowed or you may lose the stipend. Only one session is open for registration at a time.

name: Prime Time Teen (PTT)
org: City of Sacramento Youth, Parks and Community Enrichment
pay_detail: $325 stipend and certificate.
duration: 8 weeks (fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 5, two class schedules)
deadline_text: Fall 2026 registration opened Aug 17, 2026. Summer 2027 sessions: details to come.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, in middle or high school, living in Sacramento city limits. 18-year-olds need a school transcript. May complete up to two times.
how_to_apply: Make a parent or guardian ActiveNet account and register. Teen and parent must attend a mandatory orientation. PrimeTimeTeen@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Fall sessions are at Evelyn Moore (Mon and Wed) and Clunie (Tue and Thu) Community Centers, 4:30 to 7:00 pm. You must be 13 on the first day. Only one absence is allowed. Graduated high school seniors who are in college do not qualify.

name: Teen volunteers at Sacramento Public Library
deadline_text: Rolling. The library says processing takes about a month and placement can take 2 to 3 months.
who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. A parent or guardian must sign the application before you start. The page does not state ages; ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Teens who need school hours can ask about drop-in volunteering at a branch.
notes: Many people apply, so a spot is not guaranteed. Drop-in is the quickest way to start; scheduled volunteering needs a longer onboarding. Court-ordered hours are not accepted.

name: Summer Youth Academies
org: Sacramento State College of Continuing Education
pay_detail: Estimated cost $205 to $520 per academy.
duration: 1 week each (2026: June 22 to July 31)
deadline_text: The 2027 schedule is posted in January 2027. Online registration opens Monday, March 1, 2027. No closing date stated.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12. Academies are sorted into 7th to 10th and 9th to 12th grade groups.
how_to_apply: Choose an academy once the 2027 schedule is posted, then register online starting March 1, 2027.
notes: Offerings change each year; the page lists 2026 courses as examples. Some academies are online and some are in person, and the same course may have an online and an in-person section. Open to students entering grades 7 to 12.

name: Summer @ City Hall
org: City of Sacramento Youth, Parks and Community Enrichment with SCUSD, Twin Rivers and Natomas USD
pay_detail: $500 stipend plus 5 high school elective credits (letter of completion for other schools).
duration: 6 weeks (2027 start June 14)
deadline_text: Application opens Apr 1, 2027 and closes Apr 12, 2027. Interviews start Apr 19, orientation May 22, program starts June 14, 2027. Dates are tentative.
who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who attend a Sacramento City, Twin Rivers or Natomas high school or live in Sacramento city limits.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page when the window opens. Email summeratcityhall@cityofsacramento.org with questions.
notes: Dates are tentative. The city also runs Semester @ City Hall, a 6-week spring and fall version open to any high school student who lives or goes to school in Sacramento city limits; its dates are not posted yet.

name: Sacramento Youth Commission
pay_detail: $50 per meeting attended, according to the FAQ.
duration: 2-year term (up to 2 terms in a row). Up to 10 hours a month. Meets the 1st Monday of the month, 5:30 to 7:30 pm, in person.
deadline_text: Apply when a seat is open. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 22 at the time of appointment. You must live in Sacramento city limits or go to school there for your whole term. City employees cannot serve.
how_to_apply: Apply online for an open seat. The city clerk reviews it, then there is an orientation and a supplemental application. The Mayor nominates and the City Council approves.
notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page.

name: Zoo Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: $30 uniform fee.
duration: Jan to April 2027. 3-hour weekend shifts, at least 2 shifts (6 hours) per month
deadline_text: Applications open online Oct 10, 2026 for Zoo Teens 2027 (Jan to April). Closing date not stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, 2.75 GPA (proof needed), letter of recommendation, interview, $30 uniform fee, mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online starting Oct 10, send a recommendation letter and proof of GPA, then interview with the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027. The Summer Camp Counselor teen role (ages 15 to 19) is closed for 2026; check back next year. Animal Care Volunteers must be 18 or older.

name: Sacramento Food Bank and Family Services: Volunteer
duration: Shifts of a few hours
deadline_text: Online calendar with open shifts.
who_can_apply: Age 10 and up. Ages 10 to 15 need an adult chaperone; ages 16 to 17 need parent permission (waiver emailed after sign-up).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a shift on the online calendar; groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org. Phone 916-456-1980.
notes: Closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot are required. Full shifts do not appear on the calendar, so check back. People who received food bank services in the past 12 months cannot volunteer there. Groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org.

name: Sacramento County fire explorer, academy and high school fire pathways list
deadline_text: Varies by program. Spring 2027 for the Sacramento academy and Cosumnes Explorers.
who_can_apply: The page says programs are typically ages 14 to 20 and often need a 2.0 GPA, high school enrollment and parent consent under 18. Each program has its own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the links on the Metro Fire page and contact each program directly.
notes: Details from the programs' own pages: Sacramento Firefighter Youth Academy is free, ages 14 to 17, 9 months of Saturdays 8 am to 2 pm starting end of July, 35 spots, applications open in spring. Cosumnes Fire Explorers are ages 15 to 18 (juniors and seniors), 2.0 GPA, and applications for next school year open in spring 2027.

name: Sacramento SPCA Youth Service Projects
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Regular volunteers must be 18. Students and scouts can do community service projects without direct animal care. The page states no youth age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Community Service Application, or take the online New Volunteer Orientation. Questions: rmaier@sspca.org, 916-504-2807.
notes: You can become a regular volunteer at 18. Court-ordered hours are not offered. You will not get a confirmation after you send the application; you may start a project any time.

name: Sacramento Works for Youth (WIOA)
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.
deadline_text: Recruitment is year-round.
who_can_apply: Sacramento County youth ages 16 to 24. Federal eligibility rules apply, so ask a Job Center whether you qualify.
how_to_apply: Visit a Sacramento Works Job Center (find one on the Sacramento Works site). Staff at each center help youth access services.
notes: Designed for youth with extra barriers. Work experience is one of several services in a case-managed plan, not an open job board. Ages 16 to 24 are served, so this is mostly for older teens.

name: Sacramento Youth Center job training and volunteering
pay_detail: Not stated. Ask the center whether classes cost anything and whether job training pays.
deadline_text: No application deadline. Classes have their own start dates (for example Robotics Oct 3 and Sewing Oct 16; the page shows no year).
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. The page gives no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Register buttons on the Programs page, call 916-248-1081, or use the contact form.
notes: Open Mon to Sat, 12 to 6 pm, at 1901 Del Paso Blvd. The Cafe Paso job training cafe is marked temporarily closed, so ask whether job training spots are open. Pay is not stated.

name: Library volunteer (teens 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 years of age or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application (general, or the Reading Together and Homework Center form), pass a background check, and attend volunteer orientation and training. Opportunities are posted on Idealist. Volunteer Services: VolunteerSPPL@ci.stpaul.mn.us or 651-266-7432.
notes: Not a teen-only program; open to anyone 14 and older.

name: Right Track youth jobs (YJ1 and YJ2 summer internships)
org: City of Saint Paul Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: YJ1: at least $13.50 per hour, about 15 hours a week. YJ2: at least $16.37 per hour, 15 to 40 hours a week (as stated on the program page).
duration: 6 to 9 weeks, starting in June
deadline_text: Youth apply online February 1-28 for summer. The page does not print the year, so confirm the dates for 2027.
who_can_apply: Saint Paul residents who live in a cost-burdened household (for example, they receive SNAP or Section 8) or have a barrier to employment. YJ1: at least 14 by June 1 and no older than 19 by Aug 25. YJ2: at least 16 by June 1 and no older than 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online youth application in February (have your Social Security number, household income, a phone number and an emergency contact email ready; YJ2 needs a resume). Then attend pre-employment training in March, Career Exploration Day and interviews.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applicants for about 500 YJ1 internships (FAQ). Contact (651) 266-6363 or RightTrack@ci.stpaul.mn.us. The overview text says ages 14 to 24 across all Right Track programs; the summer teen programs are 14 to 21. Unplaced teens can join an online professional development program.

name: Heithoff-Brody High School Summer Scholars
pay_detail: Paid internship; the page does not state the rate. Transit stipends are available if you lack reliable transportation.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027 (30 to 40 hours a week)
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 1, 2026 and close Feb 15, 2027.
who_can_apply: San Diego County residents who finished their most recent semester at a San Diego County high school, are 16 by June 14, 2027, have a 2.75 GPA or higher and have finished at least one high school biology class.
how_to_apply: Online application with a resume (PDF or Word), unofficial transcript and short-answer responses. Questions: community@salk.edu.
notes: Applicants under 18 must get a work permit from their school if hired. Preferred but not required: one high school chemistry class and your own transportation.

name: High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 100 hours in the school year; 1 to 3 shifts of 3 hours per week
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. It lists a deadline of July 30, 2026 and also an application window opening June 1, 2027 (notices by July 29, 2027, interviews Aug 2 to 13, 2027). The dates conflict, so confirm.
who_can_apply: High school students at least 15 years old who are starting 9th, 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the 2026-2027 school year. Spots are limited and applicants are interviewed.
how_to_apply: Online application when the window opens, then an interview. Contact Kimberly Morrow, Volunteer Coordinator, 909-579-6794 (8 a.m. to 4 p.m.).
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: closed now and the page lists conflicting dates. Non-graduating volunteers who finish 100 hours can return the next year.

name: Library Teen Leadership Program (LTLP) and Teen Volunteers
city: San Bernardino County, CA (32 branch libraries)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: One LTLP meeting a month, Aug 2026 to May 2027
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Candidates are told the result within 4 to 6 weeks. Meetings are listed from Aug 2026 through May 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 anywhere in San Bernardino County. LTLP is required for all teen volunteers at the county's 32 branches.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and turn it in at your local branch library. Then attend one meeting a month at Apple Valley, Chino Hills, Crestline, Fontana, Hesperia, Highland, Phelan or Yucca Valley.
notes: Meetings are the 2nd Thursday of the month 4 to 6 p.m. or the 3rd Saturday 10 a.m. to noon; you pick any listed date and branch. Locations may change with participation. The County Library is separate from the City of San Bernardino Public Library.

name: Sheriff's Explorer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. No fees listed.
duration: At least 8 volunteer hours a month; monthly business meetings
deadline_text: No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20, enrolled in or graduated from high school, 2.0 GPA or better, legal U.S. resident, good health and character, no arrest or conviction record and no pending cases. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian to sign a liability release.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Sheriff's Volunteer Application Form and bring it to your local station or email it to the address on the form. Contact: volforces@sbcsd.org, (909) 252-4100.
notes: Members must keep current CPR and First Aid certification and finish Explorer Academy within a year. The page does not give meeting days or locations.

name: SPARK Summer Youth Employment Program (San Bernardino County)
org: County of San Bernardino Human Resources
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour in 2026 (about 28 hours a week).
duration: 2026: about six weeks, June 15 to July 24, Monday to Friday
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened March 16 and closed at the first 800 applications or March 27, whichever came first. 2025 applications opened March 15. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: San Bernardino County residents ages 16 to 24 by the start date, legally authorized to work in the U.S., with a valid California ID card. Under 18 needs an approved work permit before day one.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the county's job site when the window opens in March, upload proof of age and residency, attend orientation, then get matched to a job.
notes: Very fast: the 2026 posting closed after 800 applications. Check hr.sbcounty.gov/spark-syep/ in early March 2027 and have proof of age, residency and a California ID ready. The county page shows a PDF on how to apply.

name: San Bernardino County WIOA Youth Programs (Youth Forward)
org: San Bernardino County Workforce Development Board
pay_detail: Work experience is one of the services. Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings depend on each provider's capacity, so call the provider that serves your city.
who_can_apply: Eligible youth ages 16 to 24. Specific eligibility rules are given by each provider.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the county's youth page. Openings depend on each provider's capacity.
notes: This is the year-round option when the summer SPARK program is closed. Phone numbers for each provider are on the county page. The page does not say whether 16 and 17 year olds are paid, so ask the provider about work permits.

name: Recreation Aide and Pool Guard (City of San Diego Aquatics)
org: City of San Diego Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: Hourly pay is not stated on the page; see the posting on governmentjobs.com.
duration: Flexible hours that work around school and sports
deadline_text: Year-round hiring. Pool Guard hiring events are monthly; Recreation Aide interviews are quarterly.
who_can_apply: Recreation Aide: at least 15 and a half years old. Pool Guard: at least 16 at the time of application, no certification needed.
how_to_apply: Apply for 'Recreation Aide' or 'Pool Guard 1' on the City's governmentjobs.com portal. The City then sends interview and skills-test details.
notes: The page does not say whether a work permit is needed; ask the City when you apply.

name: Teen Service Learner
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.
duration: Flexible hours, weekdays and Saturdays
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Ask your branch.
who_can_apply: Teens, generally ages 12 to 17. The exact age range varies by branch, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Ask a staff member at your San Diego County Library branch how to sign up.
notes: Run by the County library system, which is separate from the City of San Diego Public Library. The page lists no teen requirements; the background check and medical exam it mentions are for adult volunteers. Confirm your branch's age range before going.

name: Camp Aides (Youth Volunteers)
org: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
deadline_text: Page says recruitment for camp aides begins in May. No 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: See the museum's main volunteer page and Volunteer Application link, or contact the museum at 619-232-3821.
notes: The page gives no application steps beyond pointing to the volunteer application. Ask the museum about the time commitment.

name: Teen Team Program Assistant
org: San Diego Public Library (City of San Diego)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time through the City volunteer system.
who_can_apply: Teenagers only. The library's general volunteer rule is that volunteers must be at least 13. Annual volunteer training is required.
how_to_apply: Open the library volunteer opportunities link, pick the Teen Team Program Assistant listing, click the information icon, then 'Fill in an Application'. Sign in or create a MyImpact account and submit. If your branch has no listing, email LibraryVolunteer@sandiego.gov.
notes: Applies to City of San Diego library branches only. San Diego County Library is a different system (see the Teen Service Learner card). The page does not say how many hours a week. Background check and mandated reporter training are listed only for volunteers 18 and older.

name: San Diego Workforce Partnership youth career services
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.
who_can_apply: Free career centers. The page says it has helped thousands of 16 to 24 year olds and states no eligibility age, so ask.
how_to_apply: Complete the online program application (10 to 15 minutes). The team follows up about next steps.
notes: The programs page also lists GenAI, workforce support for in-school youth across San Diego County school systems, and EXCEL for in-school and out-of-school young adults in the South Bay; their ages and dates were not checked. Pay and permit rules for under-18 placements are not stated.

name: San Jose Middle College (San Jose City College)
org: San Jose Unified School District with San Jose City College
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors. The application needs an administrator recommendation, a teacher recommendation (core subjects), a parent questionnaire, a student questionnaire and an unofficial transcript, plus a 504 plan if applicable. The page does not say whether students outside San Jose Unified may apply.
how_to_apply: Deliver the application packet (administrator and teacher recommendations, parent and student questionnaires, unofficial transcript) to the Middle College office, Business Building B-107, San Jose City College. Questions: Lisa Canton, lcanton@sjusd.org, 408-298-2191 ext. 3996.
notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Book Reviewer)
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The page lists teen programs for ages 12 to 18. A minimum age for general volunteering is not stated. Sign up through the volunteer page and an orientation (on-site or virtual).
how_to_apply: Use "Sign Up to Volunteer" on the library volunteer page and the Better Impact system, and attend an orientation. Email volunteer@sjlibrary.org.
notes: Teen Book Reviewer roles are listed on Better Impact. See also the separate Teens Reach card. The Teens Reach card appears to describe the same program, and the age range differs between pages (12 vs 13), so confirm with the library.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.
who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages I read. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
duration: Two-year term
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20, must live in the district they represent, two-year term (up to two terms), meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Fill out the District Youth Advisory Application for the YAC. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.

name: San Leandro Library Teen Volunteers
duration: At least 4 months
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who can commit to a regular weekly shift for at least 4 months. You must attend one orientation each school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online, attend an in-person orientation at the Main Library, sign the waiver, and commit to a regular shift. Returning volunteers must use their old MyImpact login.
notes: The page mentions both 2026 and January 2026 timing, so confirm the next cycle with the Teen Librarian. It also says a teen should handle their own emails, because the program is meant to prepare you for a first job.

name: San Leandro Youth Advisory Commission
org: City of San Leandro Recreation and Parks
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages or grades. Ask the Recreation office.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call Recreation at 510-577-3462 or email SLRec@SanLeandro.Org.
notes: Meets at 6 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month at the Marina Community Center, 15301 Wicks Blvd. Events listed for the 2025-2026 term include the MLK Celebration and the Cherry Festival and Parade.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.
who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
duration: 6 months or 1 semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).

name: SPARK High School Internship
org: Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute
pay_detail: Described as fully paid; the page does not state an amount.
duration: 6 weeks, starting mid-June
deadline_text: Next application dates not posted on the page. Use the Request Info form or email the program director.
who_can_apply: California high school students who are at least 16 at the mid-June start. Preference goes to students living in San Diego or Imperial County. A few spots are reserved for San Diego MESA Alliance students.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Request Info' form on the SPARK page, or contact Program Director Sanjeev Ranade, PhD at cirmsparkinternship@sbpdiscovery.org.
notes: Confirm the current deadline before planning; the official page lists none. Whether a California work permit is needed is not stated on the page.

name: Santa Ana Zoo Volunteers (including Zoo Buddies)
org: Santa Ana Zoo (City of Santa Ana)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short-term: 40 hours or less (Greeter shifts Fri to Sun, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Long-term: more than 40 hours (shifts every day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: No deadline. Long-term volunteers do an online and an in-person orientation offered every other month.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old with an adult, or 15 years old on their own. Zoo Buddies is for ages 12 to 14, who must volunteer with a parent or guardian age 18 or older, and both complete the requirements together.
how_to_apply: Long-term volunteers and Zoo Buddies apply with the online volunteer application on the zoo page. Short-term volunteers contact the zoo through its Contact Us page. The zoo does not accept walk-up volunteers.
notes: Short-term needs the City of Santa Ana one-time volunteer waiver. Long-term needs the city volunteer application, a TB test and a background check. The City of Santa Ana volunteer page says volunteers under 18 must complete a minor waiver form. The Santa Ana library teen volunteer program was not listed because the only page found was from 2021.

name: Teaching Assistant Program (Santa Barbara Museum of Art)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Counts toward required community service hours.
duration: Per class or camp: Winter After-School Class Tuesdays Jan 12 to Feb 16, 2027 (3:30-5:15 PM); Spring Camp Mar 29 to Apr 2, 2027 (9 AM-3 PM)
deadline_text: Winter After-School Class: apply by Dec 29, 2026 (confirmations Jan 5, 2027). Spring Camp: apply by Mar 15, 2027 (confirmations Mar 22, 2027).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 interested in art or working with children. The program is competitive.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here links on the museum page for each class or camp. Email communityprograms@sbma.net or call 805-884-6457.
notes: The museum also runs a free SBPL x SBMA Teen Art Party for grades 7-12 (next: Jan 22, 2027 and Apr 16, 2027, Fridays 4-5:30 PM).

name: Counselors in Training (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours. $20 uniform shirt (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: At least 3 full weeks of camp (2026 camps ran June 15 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. CIT training was June 12, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Uniform shirt required: $20 (waived for teens with SNAP/Cal Fresh EBT).
how_to_apply: Fill in the online CIT application form. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. The page says summer CITs are invited back for fall, winter and spring break camps.

name: Quasars to Sea Stars (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
grades: Must be in 8th or 9th grade (or that age) to apply
pay_detail: Unpaid for the first 60 community service hours, then paid Museum employee shifts. The pay rate is not stated.
duration: 3 to 4 years; stay active year-round until graduation
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications were due April 3, 2026, with in-person interviews in April and orientation week June 21-27, 2026. The page says applications for 2026 opened Feb 1, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students currently in 8th or 9th grade with at least a 2.5 GPA who can give 20 hours a month in the school year and 25 hours a week in summer, and have reliable transportation to the Museum and Sea Center.
how_to_apply: Online application, then an in-person interview. Contact Teen Programs Manager Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Only 8th and 9th graders can apply, so start early. Summers are intensive. Dates shown are the 2026 cycle; expect a similar early-spring deadline next year and check the page.

name: VolunTEENS (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours for the SBUSD graduation requirement. Uniform shirt purchase required (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: Up to 16 two-hour weekend shifts, Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day (2026: May 23 to Sept 6)

how_to_apply: Fill in the online VolunTEEN application. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to reopen around April 1, 2027 (the page did not say).

name: Junior Counselor Program (Parks and Recreation)

pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer service hours.

how_to_apply: Use the Register button on the Teens and Early Adults page.
notes: The same page also lists a Job Apprentice Program and a free Arts Alliance mentoring program; those pages gave no ages or pay, so they are not listed.

name: Parks and Recreation Seasonal Jobs (lifeguard, camp staff)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Hourly, set by position. A March 2024 City notice listed $18.78 to $23.92 an hour for lifeguards, camp counselors and swim instructors; check the current posting.
duration: Summer camps and pools; aquatics hires through the year with more hiring before summer
deadline_text: Aquatics hires year-round; summer hiring is announced in the spring (March 2025 release: tryouts and interviews in April, training before June).
who_can_apply: Eligibility varies by position. Some need experience or certifications (for example lifeguard); others are for first-time workers. Camp Recreation Assistants need no experience. Minimum ages are set in each job posting and were not read.
how_to_apply: Apply to open positions on the City's NEOGOV job site (Parks and Recreation). Lifeguard jobs include a tryout.
notes: The City has offered a reduced-cost lifeguard certification course for ages 15 and up (March 2024 notice, $50 for residents); check sbparksandrec.santabarbaraca.gov for the current course. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district.

name: Teen Job and Volunteer Fair (Santa Barbara Public Library)
pay_detail: Free to attend.
duration: One afternoon, 2 hours
deadline_text: 2026 fair: Wednesday, April 15, 2026, 4:00 to 6:00 PM at Central Library (workshop April 22). The 2027 date is not posted; the library calls it annual.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12. Parents and guardians are welcome. No registration needed for the fair; the interview workshop needs registration.
how_to_apply: Just show up. Register separately for the Teen Interview Skills Workshop.
notes: 2026 employers included the Museum of Natural History and Sea Center, MOXI, Santa Barbara Museum of Art, Santa Barbara Zoo, City Parks and Recreation, and the Postal Service. More than 200 teens attended in 2025.

name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board (Santa Barbara Public Library)
grades: Book reviews: grades 7-12. Teen Advisory Board: high school students.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours (1 hour per book review, up to 5 reviews a month).
duration: Teen Volunteer Time: Thursdays 4:15 PM at Central Library (or Saturdays 11 AM to 12:30 PM at Eastside Library). Advisory Board: twice a month on Tuesdays, 5-6:30 PM, during the school year and once a month during the summer.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board applications are taken at the start of each school term. Teen Volunteer Time and book reviews are ongoing.
who_can_apply: Teens. Book reviews are for grades 7 to 12. The Teen Advisory Board is for high school students and requires a Library Services Orientation for Teens first. Volunteers ages 16 and over are welcome to complete an 8-hour training.
how_to_apply: Teen Volunteer Time: pre-register to guarantee a spot, or drop in. Advisory Board: submit the application and attend the orientation. Book reviews: submit through the library form.
notes: The apply link is the Teen Advisory Board form. Service-hour sign-off requests go to the Teen Services Librarian and take up to 3 business days. The library cannot sign court-ordered community service.

name: Teens Teach Tech (Santa Barbara Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid. About 52 community service hours in total.
duration: November 2026 to June 2027, about 2 hours a week (schedule to be set)
deadline_text: Apply by Saturday, October 24, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with strong communication skills, an interest in coding or robotics, and the ability to work well with teens and children. No experience needed. Limited spots for highly motivated teens.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the library news post).
notes: Meets at Central Library, 40 E. Anapamu St. Posted October 4, 2026, so the deadline is close. Supported by a federal library grant.

name: Dual Enrollment (Santa Barbara City College)
pay_detail: Applying to SBCC is free. High-school-based courses cost nothing. For online and campus courses, enrollment fees are waived but students pay student fees and textbooks.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Fall 2026 dual enrollment registration began July 1. Deadlines for each term are on the Dual Enrollment calendar on the SBCC page.
who_can_apply: High school and home school students. High-school-based courses are for Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students only. Some courses are restricted. Complete the SBCC application and the dual enrollment steps first.
how_to_apply: Apply to SBCC through CCCApply, then follow the Steps to Enrollment for your course type. Contact dualenrollment@sbcc.edu or 805-898-8170.
notes: Your school counselor or College and Career Center can help choose courses.

name: Sea Center Volunteers (Ty Warner Sea Center)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, Ty Warner Sea Center
pay_detail: Unpaid. A $45 program fee covers uniform, badge and administration; email scvolunteer@sbnature2.org for a fee waiver before your first training.
duration: One shift per week for at least 4 months
deadline_text: The Museum's teen page says the Sea Center accepts volunteer applications year-round.
who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 and up. Volunteers 11 to 13 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. Aquarist volunteers must be 14 or older and have done 48 hours of service first. Commit to one shift a week for at least four months.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer application, interview, then attend mandatory training. Contact scvolunteer@sbnature2.org or 805-962-2526 ext. 110.
notes: Counts for the community service hours needed to graduate from high school in Santa Barbara Unified (per the Museum). Shifts are 9:45-12:45, 12:30-3:30 or 3:00-5:00.

name: Research Mentorship Program (UCSB Summer Sessions)
grades: 10th or 11th grade (outstanding 9th graders considered case by case)
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $5,675 total ($75 application fee + $1,000 deposit + $5,600 tuition and program fees); residential $13,274 total (adds $7,599 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 8, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.
who_can_apply: High school students in 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.80. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, AP scores if any, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Competitive. Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. Residential students live on campus and housing is billed by Summer Discovery. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

name: Summer Research Academies (UCSB Summer Sessions)
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $3,475 total ($75 application fee + $900 deposit + $3,400 tuition and program fees); residential $9,874 total (adds $6,399 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 25 to July 23, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 22, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.
who_can_apply: High school students in 9th, 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.60. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. The younger, shorter and cheaper of the two UCSB pre-college programs. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

name: Santa Barbara Youth Council
pay_detail: Unpaid (the City lists compensation as none).
duration: Two-year term, July 1 to June 30. Meets the 1st and 3rd Monday at 5:15 PM at Franklin Neighborhood Center (monthly in July and August).
deadline_text: Fall 2026 City advisory group recruitment: applications due Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Applications are accepted year-round for future rounds.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19. Of 15 members, 8 must live in the City; seats are set aside for SBUSD high schools, alternative and private high schools, and at-large. Members serve two-year terms from July 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City's advisory group application. Youth Council applicants interview with both the City Council and the current Youth Council. Contact Recreation Specialist Nicole Morgan, 805-897-2582.
notes: The City's recruitment page lists Youth Council interview dates but this check did not confirm which seats are open this round, so call Nicole Morgan. The City also has a one-year Youth Intern seat on some boards and commissions (nominated by a high school principal).

name: Santa Barbara Zoo Jobs for Teens (Guest Experience Specialist and seasonal)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page; see each job listing.
duration: Seasonal, mostly spring and summer
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Zoo says the busiest hiring is a month before spring and summer school breaks.
who_can_apply: Most of our job opportunities are open to applicants 14 years and older; some positions require that an applicant be at least 16 or 18. You must be able to present proof of citizenship or legal right to work in the United States. Most positions require some related experience and/or an educational background in a related field. Students with no prior work experience: 'We will consider your application for our entry level positions.'
how_to_apply: Apply online for a specific opening on the Zoo's Employment Listings page. One application per job.
notes: The Employment Listings page was not read, so check whether any openings are posted now. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district.

name: Zoo Teen Volunteers (Junior Camp Counselor, Leader in Training, Teen Conservation Club)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.
duration: Junior Camp Counselor: 7 hours a day, Mon-Fri, 3 summer weeks plus 1 fall week and 2 winter weeks
deadline_text: No application dates are posted. The Zoo volunteer page says it is not taking new volunteer recruitment applications at this time (that line sits in the adult sign-up steps), yet the teen sections still show application links. The Leader in Training dates (June 17 to Aug 23) have no year.
who_can_apply: Current junior high or high school students. Junior Camp Counselors give at least 3 weeks of summer Zoo Camp (about 100 hours). Leaders in Training give 4 summer weeks (about 130 hours). Special-event volunteers can be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply links under Teens on the Zoo volunteer page (junior camp counselor application plus a reference letter). Call or email the Zoo to confirm before you plan.
notes: Confirm first. The Zoo says no internships are available at this time. The Zoo held a Job and Volunteer Fair on February 22 (year not on the page).

name: Santa Clara County Teen CERT Academy
pay_detail: Free
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.

name: Santa Clara Youth Commission
duration: September to May, up to six years
deadline_text: The 2026-27 recruitment is closed. The page does not give 2027-28 dates.
who_can_apply: Santa Clara residents ages 12 to 19. You cannot be employed by the City of Santa Clara.
how_to_apply: Apply during the yearly recruitment. Call the Youth and Teen Center at 408-615-3760 or email youthcommission@santaclaraca.gov to ask when it opens.
notes: Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 6 p.m. at the Youth and Teen Center, 2446 Cabrillo Ave. The page was last updated 2026-09-30.

name: County of Santa Clara Intern and Earn
org: County of Santa Clara Employment Connection
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers (tutor a K-6 student)
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor) for a similar after-school tutoring role.

name: County of Santa Clara Student Internship Program (Level I, high school)
org: County of Santa Clara Employee Services Agency
grades: High school (regular, vocational or working toward equivalency)
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).
deadline_text: No current posting for Level I. Subscribe to email alerts on the Student Intern, Level I job title or contact county departments. Applications are reviewed as departments ask and expire after 6 months.
who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor
city: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga, CA
duration: One semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older, free one afternoon Monday to Thursday from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester, and about 7 hours of training.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application on the library's volunteer page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is included. Training is online (about 7 hours). The broader card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers) also includes after-school tutoring of a kindergarten to grade 6 student.

name: Student Advisory Trustee, Schaumburg Township District Library
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: One year: October 2026 to September 2027
deadline_text: The 2026-27 term closed Aug 9, 2026. A new application period is likely in summer 2027 but has not been posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live within the Schaumburg Township District Library service area. Grade level is not stated.
how_to_apply: The page invites eligible teens to apply but does not describe the method. Watch the library's Student Trustees page or ask the Teen Department.
notes: Board meetings are the third Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., plus monthly meetings with the Teen Department. The next-cycle timing is a guess from this year's August 9 deadline.

name: Sacramento County Office of Education Career Technical Education
deadline_text: Course catalog online; no student deadline posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.

name: Volunteer Program (ages 15 and up)
city: San Diego County, CA (La Jolla, Encinitas, San Diego, Chula Vista)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours; 2 to 4 hours a week depending on age and position
deadline_text: South region (Scripps Mercy San Diego and Chula Vista): reviewed on an ongoing basis. North region (Scripps Memorial La Jolla and Encinitas, Scripps Green): applications open the first business day of April (May orientation) and of October (November orientation); applications sent outside those periods are not reviewed.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 years old. Teens apply through the same process as adults; there is no separate teen program on the page.
how_to_apply: Submit one online application and choose one site. If chosen, you complete an interview, show proof of required immunizations and attend orientation. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
notes: Drop-in or on-call volunteering is not available; you pick a regular weekly shift. The portal opens on the first business day of each month and closes when a site is full, so apply early in the month. Only submit one application.

name: Santa Clara Valley Medical Center Volunteers
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are accepted online year-round, and the office is looking for weekday morning or afternoon shifts.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must give one 4-hour shift a week for at least six months in a row and at least 100 hours. They cannot take summer-only or school-break-only volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a volunteer reference form, then interview, attend a 2-hour orientation, pass a background check and health screening.
notes: The health screening asks for proof of vaccines, a flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the last 3 months. Ask your parent to start gathering records early. Questions: vmcvolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org.

name: Teen Council
pay_detail: No stipend or fee stated on the page.
duration: October 2026 to end of June 2027; monthly meetings on Zoom with several in-person events
deadline_text: 2026-2027 application closed Oct 1, 2026 and the first meeting is Oct 14, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a similar fall cycle.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no narrower age or grade range. Space is limited to 12 teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the Teens page. Only completed forms are considered. Questions: outreach@sdmart.org.
notes: Closed right now. Check the page around late summer 2027 for the next application.

name: Youth Ocean Advocates
grades: 9 to 12 (high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Seattle Children's Hospital Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a badge and free on-site parking.
duration: Most shifts are 3 hours on the same day and time every week; at least 6 months in a row (check each role)
deadline_text: Applications open each March, July and November and stay open until positions are filled. The site lists the next open date (not read).
who_can_apply: People 16 and over for some positions and 18 and over for others. You must meet the minimum age when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open period (you have one hour to finish), complete online training and forms within 2 weeks, do a 1-hour virtual group interview, then accept a placement. Onboarding includes a Washington State background check, an in-person health screening and a 90-minute orientation. Email VolunteerServices@seattlechildrens.org or call 206-987-4655.
notes: The youth service projects page (for ages under 16, such as donation drives or junior guilds) still carries a COVID-era notice, so it may be out of date. Nearly all shifts are weekdays starting between 9am and 2pm. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
grades: Entering senior year (the page also says 'between 11th and 12th grade')
pay_detail: Paid internship; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks full time (2026: June 22 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says information on the 2027 program will be posted in November 2026.
who_can_apply: High school students entering senior year who are 16 or older by the program start, with strong scientific interest, living in Greater Seattle or nearby. Out-of-state and international students are not accepted. You must be free for all eight weeks and able to do a Zoom interview.
how_to_apply: Online application with short essays, email addresses for two references (they get a recommendation link after you submit), a PDF transcript and a PDF resume. Applicants must be able to attend a Zoom interview with the selection committee.
notes: Highly competitive and designed for students without much research experience. Fred Hutch does not provide or arrange housing, and interns arrange their own transportation. In Washington there is no permit the teen carries: the employer must hold a minor work permit endorsement, and a parent/guardian (and the school during the school year) signs a parent authorization form (Parent Authorization for Summer Work if hired during summer break only) before the minor starts.

name: Seattle Parks and Recreation Lifeguard
pay_detail: Listed on the Parks summer jobs page as 'starts at $26.92' (the unit is not stated on the page).
duration: Summer-only at beaches and outdoor pools, or year-round at indoor pools
deadline_text: The last posting closed June 16, 2026. The Aquatics page says Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round, even when no posting is active.
who_can_apply: Seattle Parks summer jobs are open to ages 16 and up (18 and up for some positions). Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross Lifeguarding, First Aid and CPR/AED certification. The Red Cross course requires being at least 15 on or before the last class and passing a swim test.
how_to_apply: Get Red Cross certified. Then apply on GovernmentJobs.com when a listing is active, or email an Aquatic Application (or resume and cover letter) to parksaquatics@seattle.gov, or give it to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle indoor pool. Hired lifeguards pass a background check, a physical and the NW Lifeguard Test. Call 206-684-4078.
notes: Red Cross certifications last 2 years. The cost of the Red Cross course is not stated on the Parks pages. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply).

name: Seattle Parks Youth Employment and Service Learning: Pre-Employment Training
pay_detail: After finishing the training you may earn a $300 stipend or Service Learning credit toward high school graduation. Internship pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 7 weeks, 14 hours total, offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter
deadline_text: Offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter. The page does not list current dates, so email to ask.
who_can_apply: Pre-Employment Training is for ages 13 to 18, and you can take it once every 2 years. It is the prerequisite for Parks paid internships (Teen Late Night, Summer, Community Learning Centers), which are for ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: Email PKS_Teen_Employment@seattle.gov (phone 206-684-4575) for details and to apply. The page also lists career readiness workshops (resumes, mock interviews, food handler permit help) at Teen Life Centers and community centers.
notes: Youth may do one paid internship at a time. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply). The page also mentions free college tours for Seattle Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.

name: Changemakers in Computing
org: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
grades: Washington high school students in 10th or 11th grade when applying (rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Free. Every mentee gets a $1,200 stipend; lunch and materials are provided. No housing, and bus passes are not provided.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, about 9am to 3pm (2026: July 6 to 30)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: applications opened March 4 and closed April 1, 2026 (11:59pm PT); decisions April 27; orientation May 16. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Washington state residents enrolled in a Washington high school in 10th or 11th grade. No coding experience needed. The program aims to include economically disadvantaged and future first-generation college students; the home page says it is open to all rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline (every application submitted on time is reviewed equally). Questions: cic@cs.washington.edu.
notes: Students must be able to get to the UW campus on their own. Absences are limited: after four absences students are dismissed. The stipend is described as a stipend, not a wage, so work permit is marked unknown.

name: Business and Leadership Program (UW Foster School of Business)
org: University of Washington Foster School of Business with Summer Springboard
pay_detail: Commuter tuition $4,498 (lunch, a course, excursions, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday). Residential adds $3,000. Commuters can join weekend excursions for $125 per day. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 session: July 5 to 17)
deadline_text: No deadline stated; 'spaces are limited.' The only session listed was July 5 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students (page lists rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders and graduating seniors; no age range stated). No business experience required.
how_to_apply: Apply through partner Summer Springboard's online portal (Apply now link on the program page). Program questions go to the program contact listed on the page.
notes: Expensive paid pre-college program from a real university. The page says students can attend both experiences during a single extended stay, but it does not name a one-week Business Startup Bootcamp.

name: Woodland Park Zoo Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program
grades: Entering 10th to 12th grade in the fall of the program year (2026 page)
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Marked work permit unknown because of the stipend.

name: Seattle Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Seattle Human Services Department
pay_detail: Internship: at least Seattle's minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour. Learn & Earn Foundations: $325 stipend at the end of each module. Pathways: monthly stipend, amount not stated.
duration: Internship about 6 weeks (July 6 to Aug 18, 2026). Foundations: October 2026 to March 2027 (tentative), 2-hour weekly sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 internship applications ran March 18 to May 5, 2026 (closed). Learn & Earn Foundations 2026-27 applications ran Aug 11 to Sept 25, 2026 (closed). 2027 dates are not posted.
