how_to_apply: Apply on volunteer.stanfordhealthcare.org. Questions: VolunteerResources@stanfordhealthcare.org or 650-723-7424.
notes: Stanford says this does not count for school clinical-hour needs and has no shadowing.

name: Stanford Clinical Summer Internship (MEDCSI)
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $6,580 on campus, $4,580 virtual, $2,480 for the 10-week fall virtual option. Application fee $95 for summer ($75 fall). Fee waivers for U.S. citizens or green card holders under $80,000 household income or in low-income support programs, limited and first come first served.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 13 to 24 on campus; July 27 to Aug 7 virtual)
deadline_text: All 2026 programs closed. The page says the next cycle opens Jan 1, 2027; no 2027 deadline posted. Last cycle: Nov 1, 2025 to Feb 9, 2026.
who_can_apply: 16 by start; strongly suggested to have taken high school biology. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores, essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the MEDCSI SlideRoom portal when the new cycle opens. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores (if available), essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
notes: Pay-to-play and expensive. Fees shown are 2026 prices. No stipend or work experience. The program also admits undergraduate pre-med students.

name: Pediatrics Internship Program at Stanford (PIPS)
pay_detail: No fee. $3,000 stipend for students who show financial need.
duration: 7 weeks, 30 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Feb 23, 2026 (decisions Apr 1, 2026). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors, 16 or older, unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher, living in and attending high school in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Alameda, Contra Costa or Santa Cruz County. You must live with a family member or legal guardian; housing and transportation are not provided.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the PIPS portal when the next cycle opens. Check the PIPS page for the next cycle.
notes: About 35 to 40 students are admitted. The page says in person, with some remote work possible. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.
duration: Two weeks, live online (2026: June 15 to 26 or July 6 to 17)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Mar 13, 2026 (decisions mid-May 2026). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Currently in grades 8 to 11 and between 13 and 19 years old during the program dates. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts and the application fee; rank up to three courses. Financial aid is a separate form due about a week after the deadline.
notes: Pay-to-play. Prices and dates are from 2026. The page says to join the mailing list for future dates. Age wording on the admissions page is 'between 13 and 19'.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
grades: Juniors and seniors (classes of 2027 and 2028 for the 2027 program)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: the 2026 application fee was $50 (waivable for family income under $80,000). No program cost. Most students get no stipend; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist.
duration: 8 weeks, about 40 hours a week, tentatively June 7 to July 29, 2027
deadline_text: Application opens Dec 18, 2026 at 5pm Pacific; due late February 2027 (exact date not posted). 2026 deadline was Feb 21, 2026.
who_can_apply: Juniors or seniors now (classes of 2027 and 2028), 16 or older by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the U.S., and a U.S. citizen or green card holder. Local Bay Area students are strongly favored. You must live with a family member or guardian.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts and recommendations. In 2026 the decision date was Apr 10.
notes: Very competitive. Housing and transportation not provided. Fee and decision date shown are from the 2026 cycle.

name: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
pay_detail: Tuition free. Housing and stipend not stated.
duration: About 5 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 26)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who are low-income and first-generation college students living in Northern California. About 24 students are admitted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the SlideRoom link on the SMYSP page when it opens. Contact: smysp-team@stanford.edu.
notes: The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

name: City of Sunnyvale Youth Volunteer Program
deadline_text: Ongoing. Roles are posted as needed.
who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. Most roles require volunteers 18 and older to be fingerprinted and cleared first, so ask which roles take teens.
how_to_apply: Fill one application: general, library, or recreation and senior center. Volunteer Resources: 408-730-7533.
notes: Official page read directly. Fill out only one application.

name: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (SVCTE)
org: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (Metropolitan Education District)
fields: arts-media; engineering; food-hospitality; health; tech-cs; trades
pay_detail: Not stated. Dual enrollment courses earn college credit. The site links a Schedule of Fees page that was not read, so ask about costs.
deadline_text: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your counselor for enrollment dates.
who_can_apply: The pages read do not list eligibility rules. Shadow Days require your home school counselor's approval. Ask your counselor or call SVCTE about enrollment.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor about enrolling in SVCTE courses. To visit, apply for a Shadow Day through the SVCTE site (your counselor must approve it). Phone (408) 723-6403, Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. The site lists Milthon Marquez as Post-Secondary Planning Coach.
notes: Re-read the SVCTE home page and the Shadow Days, Dual Enrollment, Internships and Post-Secondary Options pages on 2026-10-07. The homepage lists 22 career technical courses (the old file said more than 24 pathways). Dual enrollment courses are taught by college professors at the high school campus. Shadow Days: after talking to your home school counselor, submit interest on the site; the counselor must approve it, and you get a confirmation 7 days before the visit. Eligibility, costs, deadlines and enrollment dates are not stated on the pages read.

name: Dual Enrollment at Technical College System of Georgia colleges
org: Technical College System of Georgia (including Atlanta Technical College)
pay_detail: No tuition, fees or books for the first 30 hours for eligible students. Not a paid job.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
deadline_text: Each college sets deadlines. Atlanta Technical College lists June 1 for fall, Nov 1 for spring and April 1 for summer (no year stated).
who_can_apply: Students at a participating Georgia high school or approved home study program. 11th and 12th graders and returning 10th graders can take any approved course. New 10th graders take career courses, or core courses with the required SAT or ACT score. 9th graders can join but get no state funding.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school and parent or guardian, apply to the college, and apply for dual enrollment funding at GAfutures.org. Atlanta Tech asks for PSAT, SAT, ACT or Accuplacer scores (a 2.6 HOPE GPA can be used for 11th and 12th graders).
notes: Atlanta Tech funding rules on its page: 15 funded hours per semester, a 30 hour total, and funding ends after two course withdrawals. Atlanta Tech high school contact: hsadmissions@atlantatech.edu or 404-225-4511. This is a course program, not a job, so no work permit applies.

name: The Tech Interactive Teen Volunteer Program (Holiday Helper)
deadline_text: Applications open Oct 9 to Oct 23, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page states no minimum age or other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer hub during the window. Questions: volunteer@thetech.org or 408-294-8324.
notes: Very time-sensitive: the window is two weeks. Check with the museum about age rules before applying.

name: Summer Junior Volunteer Program (North Austin)
grades: Enrolled in high school for the following school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: About 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 1 to June 25 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 application opened Monday Feb 9 and closed Friday Feb 13, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 by June 1 of the program year and enrolled in high school for the next school year. The flyer describes the program as ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, upload two recommendation letters from two different references, and upload your most recent report card. Accepted volunteers must show vaccine records (MMR, varicella, Tdap) and a negative TB test, and attend mandatory orientation on the first two days.
notes: The flyer calls the program prestigious and highly sought-after, so expect competition. Up to two absences are allowed and there are no weekend or make-up shifts. Questions: ATXNCVolunteerServices@texaschildrens.org or 737-229-3388. Check the Texas Children's volunteer pages for the 2027 flyer.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: Travis County Health and Human Services with Austin Public Health
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page
duration: not stated
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed and the page is labeled Expired. 2027 dates are not posted; the county has a 2027 interest form to get notified when applications open.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590. Pay rate, hours and program length are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page).

name: Tri-Valley ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
fields: trades; health; tech-cs; engineering; education; law-government
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is closed. Talk to your school's College and Career Specialist or counselor.
who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.

name: Trybe Summer Jobs and Paid Internships (East Oakland)
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).
duration: About 100 hours
deadline_text: No current dates posted. The old 2022 posting took applications until May 31.
who_can_apply: Current rules are not posted. Older postings (2022) said 16 and up with photo ID; confirm with the program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program
duration: 8-week program, 6-week minimum (2026: June 15 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application completion deadline May 4, 2026 (first come, first served). 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (at least one from a school mentor), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.

name: UC Davis Medical Microbiology and Immunology high school research internship
org: UC Davis School of Medicine with DJUSD and Esparto CTE
pay_detail: The DJUSD CTE page says its internships are unpaid. The UC Davis article does not mention pay.
duration: 10 weeks (2025 cohort: Mar 18 to May 22)
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort not confirmed. Last known cohort ran Mar 18 to May 22, 2025.
who_can_apply: Students in career programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows a UC Davis Center for Valley Fever internship in spring.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.

name: Summer at UC Davis Pre-College Program
org: UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education
pay_detail: 2025 tuition was $6,985 plus a $100 application fee (includes dorm and meals). 2027 price not posted yet.
duration: about 2 weeks per session (2025: July 7 to 18 and July 21 to Aug 1)
deadline_text: 2025 cycle deadline was May 16, 2025 (the fee page still shows 2025). 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages: other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.

name: UC Davis Upward Bound
pay_detail: No fee listed on the page. Confirm with the program.
duration: school year plus summer
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Check with an Upward Bound advisor at your school.
who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages read, so ask.

name: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $7,750 (housing, meals and 5 units of credit included). Application fee $45 in 2026. Fee reduction and application fee waiver available.
duration: 6 weeks (2026 dates: June 21 to Aug 1)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2026, teacher references by Mar 3. 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for fee reduction by the deadline if you need it.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.

name: UC Scout Online High School Courses
pay_detail: Fees vary by course; the site mentions free options for CA public schools and scholarships (prices not on the home page)
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Fall 2026 enrollment is open (as of Oct 7, 2026).
who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.

name: COSMOS at UC Irvine (California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science)
pay_detail: Fee-based residential program. The 2027 cost is not stated on UCI's page, so check the COSMOS site for the current fee.
duration: 4 weeks, residential (2027 session dates TBA)
deadline_text: Statewide COSMOS dates: application opens Jan 6, 2027 at 8:00 AM and closes Feb 5, 2027. Financial aid forms postmarked by Feb 6, 2027. Decisions Mar 25, 2027. UCI's own pages still show 2026 dates, so confirm there.
who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement, teacher recommendation(s), transcripts and a parent or guardian e-signature, plus the application fee. You choose one campus and cluster. Pay one-third of tuition by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027 if accepted.
notes: Competitive: about 160 to 200 students per campus. UCI says the 2027 application will be available in January 2027 and to watch for info sessions in December. Students must live on campus for the full program. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses; this card is the UC Irvine campus.

name: UCI Health High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One 3-hour shift a week, Monday to Friday 4 to 7 p.m., minimum 75 hours
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are currently closed. The page says it is under construction and will be back soon, with no date.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and over. Selection looks at your application, your ability to keep the weekly schedule, past community service, and your education and career interests.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps. Email ucimcvolunteer@uci.edu or call 714-456-5541 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: Requires a physician-signed medical clearance with immunity proof (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Tdap, hepatitis B series, COVID-19 vaccine with booster, flu shot in season, and a negative TB blood test within 90 days of your start date. Also a three-hour orientation.

name: UCLA Summer Sessions for high school students
pay_detail: Fee-based. Ask UCLA Summer Sessions for current fees. Scholarship programs described on the page include BASE and Summer Scholars Support.
duration: Focus Series: 3 weeks; other formats vary (2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 31)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 enrollment is closed. Summer 2027 programs and dates are not posted yet; the site offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each program page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.

name: UCR TRIO Pre-College: Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply with the interest form or ETS application.
who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to receive an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application and give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu; phone (951) 827-7863.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.

name: COSMOS at UC San Diego
org: UC San Diego (Jacobs School of Engineering) / California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
deadline_text: 2027 applications open Jan 6, 2027 at 8 a.m. and close Feb 5, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. The program says no exceptions to the deadline.
who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.

name: Sports Medicine Summer Academy (Research Scholars)
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 summer enrollment closed June 26, 2026; fall 2026 enrollment closed Sept 21, 2026. Summer 2027 dates not posted; you can sign up for notifications on the program page.
who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page (add the course to your cart). No application or essay. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.

name: UCSF Health Volunteer Program (includes BCH Oakland campus)
org: UCSF Health / UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals
city: Oakland, CA (BCH Oakland) and San Francisco
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months
deadline_text: Page update dated Sept 22 (year not stated): registration opens Tuesday Oct 13 at 9:30am only for two high-need SF programs. Other opportunities, including others at BCH Oakland, are listed as full.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.

name: ESTEEM/SER-Quest Summer Program
org: A. James Clark School of Engineering, University of Maryland (Center for Minorities in Science and Engineering)
pay_detail: No cost to students selected (stated on the page). No stipend is stated.
duration: 4 weeks (Jul 7 to Jul 31 in 2026), commuters only
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application deadline Mar 29, 2026; teacher recommendations due Apr 9, 2026; program Jul 7 to Jul 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.

name: Terp Young Scholars
org: University of Maryland, College Park (Extended Studies)
pay_detail: 2026 package fee: $1,791 campus option or $1,420 online option (3 credits, tuition and fees). Also a $75 application fee and a $275 program deposit that is credited to the bill. Partial scholarships, none above 30% of the package fee.
duration: 3 weeks (Jul 13 to Jul 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: Application window dates are not stated on this page. The page says the application for this year is currently closed.
who_can_apply: Page lists rising 10th through graduating 12th grade; minimum age 13 and the 3.0 GPA rule are not stated on this page.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and the campus or online option, then apply online with a transcript, health insurance card and card payment for the application fee and deposit. No essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.

name: Teen Counselor-in-Training (CIT) program
pay_detail: One-time $100 registration fee (orientation, training, t-shirt, certificate, supplies); financial aid available for students who qualify for free or reduced school lunch. CIT service is volunteer time.
duration: Flexible half or full days over the summer
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 are closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for the next session; an info session is held each February and the 2026 orientation was June 12.
who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.

name: Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) Camp
org: University of Minnesota, Minnesota CAV program
pay_detail: Free to attend; lunch is provided
duration: One week, day camp
deadline_text: Information about the 2027 camp will be available in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application instructions for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.

name: National Summer Transportation Institute (NSTI)
org: University of Minnesota Center for Transportation Studies
pay_detail: Free two-week day camp
duration: Two weeks, day camp
deadline_text: Dates and application instructions for the 2027 camp will be announced in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.

name: Explore@UNC
pay_detail: $625 per student per week (includes a $50 non-refundable registration and placement fee); some tracks may add a $25 activity fee; lunch and snacks included. Need-based aid for permanent NC residents who are rising seniors.
duration: 1 week. 2027 weeks: June 14-18, June 21-25, June 28-July 2, July 12-16. Commuter only, no residential option.
deadline_text: Pre-registration runs mid-December 2026 through mid-January 2027; placement notices early February 2027; financial aid paperwork due January 28, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.

name: Union City Youth Commission
duration: August to May
deadline_text: The page lists applications from February 1 to April 1, interviews in April and appointments in May. It gives no year, so treat this as last year's pattern.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.

name: U.S. Senate Page Program
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
deadline_text: Padilla's office: opens Oct 13, 2026, closes Oct 26, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session.
who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or rising junior or senior (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office at Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Only about 30 positions in the whole Senate. Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.

name: United States Senate Youth Program
org: Hearst Foundations, with the California Department of Education
grades: Juniors and seniors (rising juniors and seniors may apply)
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
deadline_text: California's deadline for the 2027 program is October 7, 2026 (today, as of this check). If you miss it, the next cycle is expected in fall 2027. States must report delegates by Dec 1, 2026.
who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.

name: USC Summer Programs (pre-college)
org: University of Southern California, Summer Programs
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines were May 8 for domestic and March 13 for international applicants. 2027 dates and prices are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page read does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.

name: USS Hornet Museum Volunteer (ages 16 and up)
org: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.

name: SEES (STEM Enhancement in Earth Science) Summer High School Intern Program
org: UT Austin Center for Space Research with NASA and the Texas Space Grant Consortium
pay_detail: No stipend. Free for scholarship recipients and for virtual participation; paid participants pay $2,000 tuition (meals, housing, tours and local travel included, travel to Austin not included). Travel scholarships are available.
duration: Online work in June and July plus a 2-week on-site session in Austin (July 5-18 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline: February 22, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. PT, no late applications. 2027 dates are not posted; the page says future funding is not guaranteed.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.

name: Longhorn Engineering Summer Camp (LESC)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $75 commitment fee for Austin participants, collected only after acceptance (day camp, no lodging)
duration: 4 days (Austin sessions June 8-11 and July 6-9 in 2026; both were full)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026 closed March 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.

name: My Introduction to Engineering (MITE)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $200, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)
duration: 5 days (June 21-25 and July 12-16 in 2026)
deadline_text: Applications for MITE 2026 closed March 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.

name: UVA Advance Pre-College Program
org: University of Virginia Summer and Special Academic Programs
pay_detail: The FAQ says the maximum aid package covers full tuition and fees for Virginia residents, which is $7,097 for 2026. The cost for other students and the full breakdown were not read. Small number of need-based aid packages.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 11 to August 7), residential
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened December 1; deadline March 1, 2026; teacher recommendation March 4; decisions March 31; accept by April 15. No 2027 dates posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.

name: UVA Health Junior Volunteer Summer Program
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 8 to July 31); at least 50 hours, or one full weekday, with at least 6 weeks of service
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: interest form due February 20, 2026; info sessions February 25 and March 7, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school youth ages 14 to 18. Students must attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian and an all-day orientation on the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Submit the online interest form, attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian, then interview if selected. Two references must complete the online reference form before the interview.
notes: The program page mentions a lottery. Cost and immunization rules for juniors were not stated on that page; UVA Health's general volunteer page lists a health assessment, vaccination requirements, background check and training for volunteers. Questions: 434-924-5251.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join; volunteers over 100 hours can be considered for scholarships through community partners (2024 flyer).
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2024: June 17 to July 26)
deadline_text: The VA page says applications for the 2026 program closed April 24, 2026. The 2024 deadline was April 30. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.

name: Valley Water Youth Commission
org: Valley Water (Santa Clara Valley Water District)
city: San Jose, CA (serves all Santa Clara County)
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month
deadline_text: The application is closed and will open again in Spring 2027. Fill out the interest form to be told.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.

name: Art Exchange (Vancouver Art Gallery and Arts Umbrella)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Arts Umbrella
pay_detail: Free to students (full scholarship). Not a paid job.
duration: October 2026 to June 2027
deadline_text: Submissions for the 2026-27 program were due Tuesday, September 29, 2026 at 8 AM. Next cycle not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens aged 13 to 15. Applicants send a portfolio (5 to 7 finished works and 3 to 5 sketchbook images, 10 images total) and a letter of intent of 500 to 1,000 words.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the page to submit the portfolio and letter of intent. Questions: submissions@artsumbrella.com or 604-681-5268.
notes: Scholarship-funded learning program, not a paid job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: Teen Art Group (Vancouver Art Gallery and Emily Carr University)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Emily Carr University of Art + Design
grades: Aged 15 to 18 or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026

deadline_text: Registration for fall 2026 is open (no closing date stated). The scholarship deadline was September 15, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students aged 15 to 18, or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Emily Carr University Continuing Studies website (Apply Now link on the page). Questions: teens@ecuad.ca.
notes: Paid-for arts program, not a job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: Youth Employability Program (BGC South Coast BC)
pay_detail: Participants are paid to take part, with a completion bonus for finishing all 8 weeks. Amounts are not stated on the page. Free to join.
duration: 8 weeks per session
deadline_text: Sessions run every other month (the page gives Oct, Dec, Feb, Apr as examples) and recruiting starts one month before each start date. No events were listed when read.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 30 who need to find work. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Click an event under Upcoming Events on the page to apply. Central office: 604-879-6554 or info@bgcbc.ca. Seats are limited.
notes: Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet. The page did not say where the workshops are held.

name: Science World Volunteer Program
grades: Grades 11 and 12 for the High School Work Experience placement
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.
duration: 100 hours minimum, one 2 to 3 hour shift per week
deadline_text: The core volunteer intake is closed; intake and training sessions are scheduled each year. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: Core volunteer program: at least 16 years old, 100 hours minimum. High School Work Experience: Lower Mainland students in Grades 11 and 12; teachers sign students up.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page for the next intake. For the work experience placement, ask your teacher to sign you up.
notes: The Science World Teen Advisory Group (ages 16 to 18) is on hiatus and not taking applications (page read 2026-10-09). Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: SFU Camps Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get volunteer hours, evaluations, confirmation letters and a reference request option.
duration: Minimum 2 weeks (at least 80 hours), consecutive or separate
deadline_text: 2026: online applications opened March 20 and closed April 20, 2026; interviews mid-May (in person); training late June. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 years of age by June 29, 2026. If accepted, you submit a criminal record check and complete training.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application, attend one in-person interview, then complete in-person or online training. Returning volunteers can apply as Lead Volunteers by email.
notes: SFU Camps says it is not a registered non-profit; check with your teacher that your school accepts these hours for service or work experience credit. Top volunteers are encouraged to apply as paid instructors later (2026 instructor wage $27.05 to $28.50 per hour, CAD); the minimum age for instructors is not stated on the page. Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: Stanley Park Ecology Youth Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can request a reference letter after 25 hours.
duration: Varies by role; many are seasonal
deadline_text: Varies by role: DIRT and Nature House Host take applications year-round when there is room; EcoRangers apply in May; EcoCamp Assistant applications open in February and May; EcoStewards is listed as open.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17 can join EcoStewards, DIRT, Nature House Hosts, EcoRangers and EcoCamp Assistants. Ages 12 to 16 can join EcoStewards with adult supervision. A parent or guardian must sign the youth consent form.
how_to_apply: Register and sign up through Better Impact. If a role is closed, fill in the Volunteer Interest Form. Email vols@stanleyparkecology.ca with questions.
notes: Volunteer role in Canada. British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet, so work permit is marked unknown. Most other roles on the site are for volunteers 16 and older.

name: Museum Teen Internship (Summer Service Program)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Interns get high school service credit, a letter of recommendation, training, free parking and museum passes to share.
duration: June to August; at least 25 service hours. Gallery shifts of 2-4 hours, 1-3 times a week; camp assistants commit to a full camp week (Mon-Fri, 8:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m.)
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2026 are closed. The 2027 deadline is not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. Applicants must apply by the posted deadline, attend a short interview and orientation, and commit to at least 25 service hours.
how_to_apply: Apply by the posted deadline, then interview and attend orientation. Contact Anna Deater-Deckard, anna@vadm.org, 434-977-1025 x104.
notes: The museum is a small children's museum for infants to age 8, so the work is with young kids. Weekday and Saturday shifts are available.

name: C-Tech2: Computers and Technology at Virginia Tech
org: Virginia Tech College of Engineering, Center for Engineering Excellence and Discovery
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jun 28 to Jul 11 in 2026)
deadline_text: Page says applications for Summer 2027 open in early December 2026. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Open to rising high school juniors and seniors. The pages I read do not state a Virginia residency rule for this program (WEE VT has one).
how_to_apply: Joint application with WEE VT and UPWARDS: rank your choices, short essays (120 words each), a grade transcript, and a parent financial statement for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: Not a job, so no work permit.

name: College of Science Summer Camps (Explore Science camps)
grades: Rising 9th to 12th (Explore Science 9-10; Life and Physical Science camps 11-12)
pay_detail: 2026 price $1,150 per residential camp ($700 for the day camp for rising 7th-8th). Camp fees cover instruction, supplies, room and board; need-based scholarships are available in the application.
duration: 5 days (Sunday to Thursday)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application portal opened January 2026; deadline for first round of applications March 2. Offers of admission and scholarships made by March 16; accepted campers have until March 30 to pay fees (minus scholarships).
who_can_apply: Rising high school students in the grade band for each camp. No GPA or residency rule appears on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp application link on the College of Science camps page; apply for a scholarship inside the form. Cancellation refund minus a $30 fee until 4 weeks before camp.
notes: Explore Science rising 9-10 camp was listed as full in 2026. Questions: explorescicamp@vt.edu. Not a job, so no work permit.

name: Watford Engineering Experience at Virginia Tech (WEE VT)
org: Virginia Tech College of Engineering, Center for Engineering Excellence and Discovery
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jul 12 to Jul 25 in 2026)
deadline_text: Page says applications for Summer 2027 open in early December. No closing date posted. 2026 program ran Jul 12 to Jul 25, 2026.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are Virginia residents.
how_to_apply: Joint application with the C-Tech2 and UPWARDS summer programs: rank your choices, add short essays (120 words each) and a grade transcript, and a parent completes a financial statement used for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: The page tells families not to let the cost stop them from applying because of scholarships. Not a job, so no work permit.

name: Virtual Enterprises International
pay_detail: School/district pays (cost not public)
duration: School year
deadline_text: Depends on your school.
who_can_apply: Students at partner schools. Schools join by filling out an interest form and talking with a VEI Regional Director.
how_to_apply: Ask your school or counselor about the program. Contact info@veinternational.org or 855-740-6555.
notes: Not an individual sign-up; your school must be a partner. Cost to schools is not posted.

name: WakeMed Junior Volunteer Program (High School)
grades: High school, through the summer after graduation
duration: Minimum 6 months, one day a week on a regular set day and time
deadline_text: Applications open for only about 24 to 48 hours. The page tells students to check on the 15th of October, December, February, April, June and August. The next check date is October 15, 2026. Both applications were listed as closed on 2026-10-09.
who_can_apply: High school students age 16 or older (the page covers ages 16 through the summer after graduation). Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN and Occupational Health clearance. Apply to only one location: Raleigh Campus or Cary Hospital.
how_to_apply: Review the current junior-eligible openings, then submit the online application for one campus during an open window. Selected students interview, give two references, finish medical screenings and attend orientation.
notes: Not first come, first served. Processing takes about 3 to 5 weeks. Required Occupational Health clearance includes flu, MMR, Varicella, Tdap and TB. Not for court-ordered community service. The page describes volunteer service, not an internship or job shadowing.

name: Washington Aerospace Scholars
city: Seattle, WA (online course, then a summer residency at the Museum of Flight)
pay_detail: Phase 1 online course is free (optional 5 UW credits cost $255; financial assistance up to 100% available). Optional Phase 2 six-day residency costs $1,850 including room and board; tuition assistance up to 100% available.
duration: Phase 1: November through March (15-20 hours per two-week lesson). Phase 2: six-day residency in July or August.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications are open and close after October 13, 2026. Applicants are accepted on a rolling basis while room is available.
who_can_apply: Washington state residents who are high school juniors (per the 2025 WAS FAQ: 'Scholars must be a Washington state resident and be a current junior in high school'). No math or science prerequisites are listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WAS 2026-27 Program Application linked on the program page. Questions: WAS@museumofflight.org or 206-768-7214. Phase 2 invitations use a lottery among students who meet the Phase 1 requirements.
notes: Deadline is very close. Graduates can apply for Museum scholarships. Participation in Phase 2 is not required for Phase 1. Students who are not juniors yet can fill out the Program Interest Form on the page to be contacted when they are eligible.

name: Washington Health (Fremont) High School Volunteer Program
deadline_text: Next high school round is Fall 2026. The waiting list closed May 22, 2026, but new students can still join and are contacted only when an info session is scheduled.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont.

name: Running Start
org: Washington State Board for Community and Technical Colleges
pay_detail: No tuition. Students and families pay mandatory fees, books and transportation.
duration: Per quarter or semester
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the SBCTC page; they vary by college.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Washington. The SBCTC page does not list other requirements; contact the college's Running Start coordinator.
how_to_apply: Contact the Running Start coordinator at the college you want to attend (the SBCTC page links a coordinator list) and your high school counselor.
notes: Work hours tie-in from Washington L&I: 16 and 17 year olds enrolled in a bona fide college program, such as Running Start, may work non-school week hours during the regular school year (employers should ask for proof such as a college transcript).

name: Teen Heroes
org: City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Free to join, unpaid. The page does not list a stipend.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Dates for the next summer are not posted.

how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.

name: West Valley College Concurrent Enrollment
pay_detail: Free (per the college page)
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Follow the college's term dates.

how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.

name: Wikipedia Editing

duration: Whenever you want

how_to_apply: Start editing, or make a free account (not required). Try The Wikipedia Adventure tutorial.
notes: Protect your personal info; do not share your school or address.

name: Woodland Community College Dual Enrollment (Yolo Community College District)
pay_detail: Free up to 11 units ($46 per unit fee waived); books may cost

deadline_text: Rolling by term.

how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.

name: Teens Helping Seniors
deadline_text: No dates on the Teen Programs page.

notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

name: work2future Young Adult Program
pay_detail: Paid work experience; the page says earn up to $25 an hour. Other services are free.
deadline_text: Enrollment is open year-round.

how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program for ages 14 to 29, is also listed on the page. Income and barrier rules apply. Job centers may be open by appointment only.

name: workNet DuPage Youth Program

duration: Not stated

how_to_apply: Click Apply Now or Get Started at worknetdupage.org/job-seekers/get-started/, or call 630-955-2030. Career Center: 2525 Cabot Drive, Suite 302, Lisle.
notes: Starts at 17, so it fits only older high schoolers. Spanish-speaking services are available. The Get Started page was not read, so check eligibility there.

name: Youth R.I.S.E. (Reaching Independence through Skills and Employment)
org: WorkSource Atlanta (City of Atlanta workforce board)
pay_detail: Paid work experience and internships are one service. Wage not posted on the page. Services are no cost.
duration: Year-round, no set end date
deadline_text: Year-round, first come first served. After the online orientation you have 30 days to submit all documents or your application may be closed.
who_can_apply: City of Atlanta residents ages 16 to 24 who are WIOA eligible. In-school youth are generally 16 to 21, must meet income and other criteria, and may have a barrier such as disability, English learner, foster care, homeless, justice-involved or parenting. A WorkSource Atlanta Eligibility Specialist makes the final decision.
how_to_apply: 1) Finish the online youth orientation. 2) Create a profile in the WorkSource Georgia portal and save your SID number. 3) Upload your documents. 4) Book an eligibility appointment, or email WSAYouth@AtlantaGa.Gov with subject Ready to RISE. 5) Take the My Next Move career assessment. 6) Eligibility review.
notes: Eligibility is income and barrier based, so not every teen qualifies. The document list includes a Social Security card and proof of address; this is the official city workforce board, but upload documents only through the portal named on the page. Under 18 using parent documents: proof of relationship and shared address is needed. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: WorkSource Fulton Youth Services
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.
duration: Year-round
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Fulton County residents ages 16 to 24 who are interested in employment or training and meet low-income guidelines and/or have significant barriers to education or employment.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Visit the youth center at 4405 Mall Blvd., Suite 400, Union City, GA 30291, or call a career center: South Fulton 404-613-6800 (5710 Stonewall Tell Rd., Suite 160, College Park) or North Fulton 404-613-4480 (7741 Roswell Rd., Suite 205, Sandy Springs).

Teens signed up at the county's Summer Teen Hiring Fair on April 11, 2026; next year's dates are not posted. If you live inside the City of Atlanta, also look at Youth R.I.S.E. and ask which office serves your address. The county's older Summer Youth Job Training and Summer Youth Internship pages return errors now.

The same YMCA's Youth and Government program is already in ymca-silicon-valley-youth-and-government.json. Leaders in Training is also listed on the leadership page, but its age and details are not stated, so it is not a card.

pay_detail: Unpaid. $30 orientation fee covers name badge, uniform shirt and access card. Scholarships available for qualified applicants.

deadline_text: Applications open 9 a.m. Jan 1 and close 5 p.m. Jan 31 (the page prints no year; it is for the June 2027 program year, so Jan 2027). A free Program Preview is Nov 14, 10 a.m. to noon, with registration.

how_to_apply: Online application plus an essay of 2 pages or less written by the teen alone (AI-looking essays are rejected), and one recommendation from a non-family adult. Selected teens interview in person in March and attend orientation with a parent in April.
